records.change: Opening made a time clause: "when God created the universe"
records.note: A translation choice of the Masoretic grammar: GNB reads verse 1 as leading into verse 2, where the KJV makes it a complete statement that God created all things in the beginning. The Hebrew allows both; the absolute reading is the traditional one.

records.change: "man became a living soul" becomes "the man began to live"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew nephesh chayyah; the GNB drops "soul", which some read as bearing on the nature of man.

records.change: Omits "your eyes shall be opened"; "as gods" becomes "like God"
records.note: The Masoretic text has the clause; the GNB leaves it out here, though Genesis 3:7 still says their eyes were opened. Elohim can be read either as "God" or "gods".

records.change: Singular "it"/"his heel" becomes collective "her offspring"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew "seed" is grammatically singular with singular pronouns, which the KJV keeps and Christian readers take as the first promise of one Redeemer. GNB's "offspring" allows that reading but no longer points to one person.

records.change: Adds Cain's words "Let's go out in the fields"
records.note: The Masoretic text does not give what Cain said; the GNB supplies it from the Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint and Syriac.

records.change: "sons of God" becomes "heavenly beings"
records.note: A translation choice: the Masoretic text has "sons of God", which some read as angels and others as the line of Seth. GNB settles on the angelic reading where the KJV leaves the phrase open.

records.change: "My spirit shall not always strive" becomes "not allow people to live forever"
records.note: The Hebrew verb is uncertain; GNB follows the sense of the Septuagint ("remain") and reads it as a limit on lifespan. The KJV's reading, of God's Spirit striving with man, is lost.

records.change: "sons of God" becomes "heavenly beings"
records.note: As in 6:2, a translation choice that settles an open phrase in favour of the angelic reading.

records.change: "My Lord" becomes "Sirs"
records.note: The consonants can be read as a plain "my lords"; the Masoretes pointed them as the divine title Adonai, which the KJV follows. GNB treats the visitors as addressed only as men.

records.change: "my Lord" becomes "sir"
records.note: As in 18:3, the Masoretic pointing is the divine title Adonai; GNB reads it as polite address to the angels.

records.change: Omits "from the LORD out of heaven"
records.note: The phrase is in the Masoretic text; GNB drops it as repetition. Older interpreters read the LORD raining fire "from the LORD" as a distinction of persons in the Godhead.

records.change: "it shall be seen" becomes "he provides"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew verb can be read as "it will be seen" (or "he will appear") or "he will provide"; the KJV's reading is often taken of a future appearing on the mount.

records.change: "virgin" becomes "young woman"
records.note: A translation choice for Hebrew almah, the word of Isaiah 7:14. The KJV renders it "virgin" here too; Rebekah is called a virgin (betulah) in 24:16 in both versions.

records.change: "in thy seed shall all nations be blessed" becomes nations asking blessing
records.note: A translation choice taking the Hebrew verb as reflexive: nations bless themselves by Isaac's descendants. The KJV makes the seed the source of blessing, the reading Paul applies to Christ in Galatians 3:8, 16.

records.change: Blessing of fatness and dew becomes "no dew... no fertile fields"
records.note: The Hebrew preposition can mean "of" or "away from"; GNB takes the second, turning Esau's lesser blessing into a denial. Most modern versions agree with GNB; the KJV's reading is also possible.

records.change: The LORD "stood above it" becomes "standing beside him"
records.note: The Hebrew can mean above the ladder or beside Jacob; GNB takes the second. The picture of the LORD at the top of the ladder (compare John 1:51) is lost.

records.change: "terror of God" becomes "great fear"
records.note: A translation choice reading the phrase as an idiom for great terror. The KJV makes God the source of the fear that protected Jacob.

records.change: "coat of many colours" becomes "long robe with full sleeves"
records.note: The Hebrew is uncertain; the KJV follows the Septuagint's "many-coloured", GNB a guess from the word's root. Not doctrinal.

records.change: "coat of many colours" becomes "long robe with full sleeves"
records.note: As in 37:3, a different reading of an uncertain Hebrew word.

records.change: "the grave" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: A translation choice for Hebrew Sheol, which the KJV renders "grave" here and "hell" elsewhere. GNB makes it a realm of the dead rather than a burial place.

records.change: "bowed himself" becomes "gave thanks"
records.note: The Hebrew speaks of bowing (worship) at the bed's head; Hebrews 11:21 follows the Septuagint's "staff". The GNB's "gave thanks" is an interpretation of the gesture.

records.change: "digged down a wall" becomes "crippled bulls"
records.note: The consonants can be vocalized as "wall" or "ox"; the KJV reads the former, the Masoretic vowels and the GNB the latter. "O my soul" is also dropped.

records.change: Drops "until Shiloh come"; rule made unending, nations bring tribute
records.note: The GNB reads the Hebrew shiloh as "tribute to him", a revocalization; the KJV keeps it as a name long read as the Messiah, so the messianic "until" is lost.

records.change: Drops "blessings of thy father have prevailed" over progenitors'
records.note: A translation choice following an emended Hebrew text close to the Septuagint ("grain and flowers", "ancient mountains"); the Masoretic text, which the KJV follows, compares Jacob's blessings with his forefathers'.

records.change: "mount of God, even to Horeb" becomes "Sinai, the holy mountain"
records.note: A translation choice: the GNB names Sinai where the Hebrew has Horeb, taking the two as one mountain, and turns "mountain of God" into "holy mountain".

records.change: "God of thy father" becomes "God of your ancestors"
records.note: The Masoretic text has the singular "father"; the plural agrees with the Samaritan Pentateuch and Stephen's quotation in Acts 7:32. The patriarchs are still named.

records.change: "the destroyer" becomes "the Angel of Death"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew has "the destroyer"; the GNB names it an angel of death, an interpretation the text does not state.

records.change: Jethro's own words become a message sent ahead
records.note: The GNB follows the Septuagint and Samaritan reading ("behold" for "I"), making it a report rather than Jethro speaking; the Masoretic text has Jethro say it.

records.change: "thousands" becomes "thousands of generations"
records.note: A translation choice reading the Hebrew "thousands" as generations, by analogy with "third and fourth generation" in verse 5; the KJV leaves it as "thousands".

records.change: "take the name in vain" narrowed to "for evil purposes"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew "in vain" (emptily, falsely) is broader than evil use; "not hold him guiltless" becomes "will punish".

records.change: "Thou shalt not kill" becomes "Do not commit murder"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew ratsach, which usually means unlawful killing; the narrower word changes how the commandment is applied.

records.change: "unto the judges" becomes "to the place of worship"
records.note: The Hebrew ha-elohim can mean God or judges; the KJV reads judges, the GNB reads it as bringing him before God at the sanctuary.

records.change: "God deliver him into his hand" becomes "an accident"
records.note: A translation choice that drops the Hebrew's statement of God's providence in an unintended killing, putting it as mere accident.

records.change: "her fruit depart" made a lost child; harm limited to the mother
records.note: The Hebrew can mean premature birth or miscarriage; the GNB chooses miscarriage and applies "no mischief" only to the woman, which bears on how the unborn child is valued.

records.change: "blood of my sacrifice" not mentioned
records.note: A paraphrase: the Hebrew forbids offering the blood of the sacrifice with leaven; the GNB speaks of offering yeast bread at a sacrifice and drops the blood.

records.change: "filled with the spirit of wisdom" becomes "given ability"
records.note: A translation choice that removes "spirit" from the Hebrew; the gift of skill from God is kept.

records.change: Omits "to make an atonement for your souls"
records.note: The Hebrew has the atonement clause; the GNB renders it only as paying "for their lives", so the word atonement is lost.

records.change: "atonement money" becomes "tax"; atonement clause reworded
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew twice speaks of atonement for souls; the GNB has a tax and "payment for their lives".

records.change: "spirit of God" becomes "my power"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew ruach Elohim is rendered as impersonal power, losing the reference to God's Spirit. Genesis 1:2 and other verses still speak of the Spirit.

records.change: Command "consecrate yourselves" becomes statement "you have consecrated yourselves"
records.note: The GNB follows the Septuagint and Vulgate past tense; the Masoretic text, with the KJV, has an imperative.

records.change: Repeated "The LORD, The LORD God" reduced to "I, the LORD"
records.note: A paraphrase that makes God the speaker and drops the double proclamation of the divine name; the attributes that follow are kept.

records.change: Omits "whose name is Jealous"; "jealous God" becomes "tolerate no rivals"
records.note: A paraphrase that drops a name the Hebrew gives God; the idea of exclusive worship is kept.

records.change: "blood of my sacrifice" not mentioned
records.note: As in Exodus 23:18, the GNB speaks of yeast bread at a sacrifice and drops the Hebrew's "blood".

records.change: "spirit of God" becomes "his power"
records.note: As in Exodus 31:3, the Hebrew ruach Elohim is rendered as impersonal power, losing the reference to God's Spirit.

records.change: "shall be holy" becomes "will be harmed by its holiness"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew says whoever touches them becomes holy; the GNB interprets this as harm from holiness, which the text does not state.

records.change: "cut off from his people" becomes "no longer considered God's people"
records.note: The Hebrew "cut off" may mean death or divine judgment; the GNB reads it as exclusion from the people, a milder penalty.

records.change: "stand against the blood of thy neighbour" becomes "testify to help him"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew forbids standing against a neighbour's life; the GNB makes it a duty to speak up at a trial, an interpretation.

records.change: One who "hath a familiar spirit" becomes one who "consults the spirits"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew condemns the medium who has the spirit; the GNB condemns those who consult one.

records.change: "cut off from my presence" becomes "never again serve at the altar"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew "cut off from before me" is read as loss of priestly service, a narrower penalty.

records.change: Names Hobab's father "Jethro" where the KJV has "Raguel"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads Reuel (Raguel); the GNB substitutes Jethro to harmonise with Exodus 3:1. A translation choice that changes a proper name, not a manuscript difference.

records.change: "Ere it was chewed" becomes "still plenty of meat"
records.note: A translation choice on the Hebrew "before it was cut off": the KJV makes the plague strike while the meat was in their mouths, the GNB while the supply lasted.

records.change: Promise that God's glory will fill earth becomes part of an oath
records.note: The Hebrew is read as "all the earth shall be filled with the glory of the LORD" in the KJV, a future promise; the GNB renders it as present fact within the oath formula. A translation choice; the promise is still stated in Habakkuk 2:14 and Isaiah 11:9.

records.change: "God of the spirits of all flesh" becomes "source of all life"
records.note: A paraphrase of a title of God, following the Masoretic text; the GNB gives its sense rather than its words, and the title recurs in Numbers 27:16.

records.change: "Who shall live when God doeth this" becomes people gathering in the north
records.note: The GNB follows an emendation of the Masoretic text in Balaam's oracle, which drops the mention of God; the KJV translates the Masoretic text as it stands.

records.change: "A man in whom is the spirit" becomes "a capable man"
records.note: A translation choice on the Hebrew ruach; the KJV reads it of the spirit given to Joshua, the GNB of natural ability. Deuteronomy 34:9 still says Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom.

records.change: "Atonement for our souls" becomes payment "so that he will protect us"
records.note: A translation choice following the Masoretic text; the GNB reads the atonement as a ransom for protection, where the KJV keeps the term of atonement before the LORD.

records.change: Omits "which was anointed with the holy oil"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text; the GNB leaves it out in its paraphrase, so the high priest's anointing is no longer mentioned.

records.change: Adds that God gave the heavenly bodies to nations "to worship"
records.note: The Hebrew says only that the LORD "divided" or allotted them to all nations; the GNB adds "for them to worship" as its interpretation. A translation choice that goes beyond the KJV's text.

records.change: Omits "in the latter days"; condition "if thou turn" becomes prediction
records.note: The Masoretic text has "in the latter days" and the KJV reads a condition; the GNB drops the phrase and says Israel "will finally turn". A translation choice that loses the eschatological note.

records.change: "Not with our fathers" becomes "not only with our fathers"
records.note: The Hebrew says the covenant was made "not with our fathers"; the GNB softens it to "not only", an interpretive addition that changes the statement.

records.change: "It shall be our righteousness" becomes "he will be pleased with us"
records.note: The Masoretic text has tsedaqah, "righteousness"; the GNB replaces the term with God's approval. A translation choice that drops a doctrinally weighted word.

records.change: "The hornet" becomes "panic"
records.note: The Hebrew tsir'ah is traditionally "hornet" (so the KJV and Septuagint); the GNB takes it figuratively as panic. A translation choice; see also Exodus 23:28.

records.change: "Lord of lords" and "terrible" become "over all powers", "to be obeyed"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew has the title "Lord of lords" and nora, "awesome, to be feared". The GNB keeps God's supremacy but drops the title and the note of awe.

records.change: "roast" the Passover becomes "Boil"
records.note: The Hebrew bashal usually means to boil or cook; the KJV reads "roast" in line with Exodus 12:9, which forbids boiling it. A translation choice that sets the two passages against each other.

records.change: "a Prophet" becomes "a prophet"
records.note: The Hebrew is the same; the KJV's capital marks the messianic reading Acts 3:22 and 7:37 apply to Christ. The GNB's lower case reads it generically, though the words are kept.

records.change: "a damsel that is a virgin" becomes "a young woman"
records.note: The Hebrew betulah, "virgin", is what the law turns on (compare Exodus 22:16); the GNB's "young woman" drops that condition. A translation choice.

records.change: "whore" and "sodomite" become "temple prostitute"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew qedeshah and qadesh, which are tied to pagan shrines; the GNB narrows the prohibition to cult prostitution.

records.change: "circumcise thine heart" becomes "give you obedient hearts"; adds "in that land"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew has the circumcision image that Romans 2:29 and Colossians 2:11 build on, and "that thou mayest live" without "in that land". The inward change of heart is still stated.

records.change: "number of the children of Israel" becomes "each nation a heavenly being"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads "sons of Israel"; the GNB follows a Dead Sea Scroll (4QDeut-j, "sons of God") and the Septuagint ("angels of God"). It makes the verse about angels over the nations instead of Israel.

records.change: "devils" becomes "gods that are not real"
records.note: The Hebrew shedim means demons; the GNB turns them into non-existent gods. 1 Corinthians 10:20 keeps the sense that idol sacrifice is offered to demons.

records.change: "the lowest hell" becomes "the world below"
records.note: The Hebrew is sheol, the realm of the dead; the GNB's rendering is a translation choice that drops the KJV's word "hell".

records.change: "I live for ever" becomes "As surely as I am the living God"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew has le'olam, "for ever", which the GNB's oath formula drops. God's being the living God is kept.

records.change: "rejoice with his people" becomes "praise the LORD's people"; land's atonement dropped
records.note: The Masoretic text can be read either way; the Septuagint's "with his people" is the reading Romans 15:10 quotes of the Gentiles. The GNB also turns "merciful unto his land" (kipper, make atonement) into forgiving the people's sins.

records.change: "a fiery law" becomes "a flaming fire"; "saints" become "angels"
records.note: The Hebrew 'eshdat is obscure; the KJV reads "fire of law", the GNB emends it to fire alone, so the giving of the law is lost from the verse.

records.change: "spirit of wisdom" becomes "wisdom"; "laid his hands" becomes "appointed"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew has ruach, "spirit", and the laying on of hands (compare Numbers 27:18-23). The GNB keeps the appointment but not the act or the spirit.

records.change: Othniel made the son of Caleb's brother Kenaz
records.note: The Hebrew "Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother" can refer to Othniel or to Kenaz; the GNB takes Kenaz as the brother, making Othniel a nephew. A translation choice; see also Joshua 15:17.

records.change: Hobab "father in law" becomes "brother-in-law" of Moses
records.note: The Hebrew chothen can mean either relation by marriage; the GNB reads brother-in-law to fit Hobab son of Reuel (Numbers 10:29). A translation choice.

records.change: "thou talkest with me" becomes "you are really the LORD"
records.note: A paraphrase choice; the Hebrew asks for a sign that it is the visitor speaking and does not name him. The GNB identifies him as the LORD, as verse 14 does.

records.change: "before the sun was up" becomes "by way of Heres Pass"
records.note: The Hebrew ma'aleh heres can mean "the going up of the sun" or "the ascent of Heres"; the GNB takes it as a place name. A translation choice.

records.change: "honour God and man" becomes "honor gods and human beings"
records.note: The Hebrew elohim can mean God or gods; the GNB takes the plural, fitting the fable. The KJV reads it as God, honoured by the oil of offerings.

records.change: "cheereth God and man" becomes "makes gods and human beings happy"
records.note: The Hebrew elohim can mean God or gods; the GNB takes the plural. The KJV reads it as God, whose drink offerings were of wine.

records.change: Omits God sending "an evil spirit"
records.note: The Masoretic text says God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and Shechem; the GNB says only that God made them hostile. The spirit sent by God also appears in 1 Samuel 16:14.

records.change: "whatsoever cometh forth" becomes "the first person"; omits "the LORD's"
records.note: The Masoretic text vows that whatever comes out shall be the LORD's and a burnt offering; the GNB makes it a person to be sacrificed. The wording bears on how Jephthah's vow is read.

records.change: "the Spirit of the LORD" becomes "the LORD's power"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew is ruach YHWH, "the Spirit of the LORD". The GNB renders it as power, so the Spirit is not named.

records.change: "the Spirit of the LORD" becomes "the power of the LORD"
