records.change: "an hollow place that was in the jaw" becomes "in the ground"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew lechi can be the jawbone or the place named after it; the GNB reads the place, so the water no longer comes from the jaw.

records.change: Jonathan's grandfather named Moses, not Manasseh
records.note: The Masoretic text has Manasseh with a raised nun, widely taken as a scribal change from Moses; some Septuagint copies and the Vulgate read Moses. The GNB follows that reading.

records.change: "going to the house of the LORD" becomes "on our way home"
records.note: The Masoretic text has "the house of the LORD"; the GNB follows the Septuagint's "my house", which fits verse 29.

records.change: "the house of God" becomes the town "Bethel"
records.note: The Hebrew beth-'el can be the town's name or "house of God"; the GNB takes it as the town where the ark then was (20:27). A translation choice.

records.change: "the house of God" becomes "Bethel"
records.note: Same Hebrew beth-'el as 20:18, read as the place name. A translation choice; they are still before the LORD.

records.change: "the house of God" becomes "Bethel"
records.note: Same Hebrew beth-'el, read as the town on the road. A translation choice.

records.change: "the house of God" becomes "Bethel"
records.note: Same Hebrew beth-'el, read as the place name. A translation choice; they are still "in the presence of God".

records.change: "shall be lightly esteemed" becomes God treating them with contempt
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew says those who despise God will be lightly regarded. The GNB makes God the one who acts against them.

records.change: "an enemy in my habitation" becomes Eli's family looking on with envy
records.note: A translation choice for obscure Hebrew: the KJV reads an enemy in God's dwelling, the GNB Eli's house troubled and envious of Israel's blessings.

records.change: "mine anointed" becomes "my chosen king"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew is mashiach ("anointed"), which many read as pointing to the Messiah. The GNB gives it a generic rendering.

records.change: Adds that they cried "to their gods"
records.note: The Masoretic text says only that the city's cry went up to heaven. The GNB adds prayer to pagan gods, which the Hebrew does not state.

records.change: "fifty thousand and threescore and ten" becomes "seventy"
records.note: The Masoretic text has 50,070; a few Hebrew manuscripts and Josephus have 70, which the GNB follows.

records.change: "for his great name's sake" becomes "made a solemn promise"
records.note: A paraphrase choice; the Hebrew grounds God's faithfulness in his own name. The GNB grounds it in a promise instead.

records.change: Omits the verse on the length of Saul's reign
records.note: The Masoretic text's numbers here appear incomplete (literally "a year old"), and the Septuagint omits the verse; the GNB leaves it out. The KJV renders the Hebrew as it stands.

records.change: "a man after his own heart" becomes "the kind of man he wants"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew describes David as a man after God's heart, a phrase quoted in Acts 13:22. The GNB keeps the sense but loses the wording.

records.change: "the ark of God" becomes "the ephod"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads "ark of God"; the Septuagint reads "ephod", which fits 14:3. The GNB follows the Septuagint.

records.change: "the evil spirit from God" loses "from God"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew says the evil spirit was from God (ruach elohim ra'ah). The GNB leaves out its source, though 16:14 still says it was sent by the LORD.

records.change: "a covenant of the LORD" becomes "the sacred promise"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads "a covenant of the LORD"; the GNB renders it without the divine name, a translation choice. The covenant's sanction by the LORD is no longer stated.

records.change: Covenant "before the LORD" becomes a "sacred promise"
records.note: The Masoretic text says the covenant was made before the LORD; the GNB drops the divine name, a translation choice.

records.change: "the LORD'S anointed" becomes "the one whom the LORD chose"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew is mashiach YHWH ("the LORD's anointed"). The GNB keeps the sense of God's choice but loses the word behind "Messiah".

records.change: Statement "evil not found in thee" becomes a prediction
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew states that no evil has been found in David. The GNB turns it into a promise that he will do no evil.

records.change: Omits "bound in the bundle of life with the LORD"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew image of the soul bound up with God, which some read of life beyond death, becomes guarding a treasure.

records.change: "the LORD'S anointed" becomes "whom the LORD made king"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew is mashiach YHWH. The GNB keeps the sense of God's appointment but loses the word behind "Messiah".

records.change: "Leaneth on a staff" becomes "fit only to do a woman's work"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew pelek can mean a crutch or a spindle; the GNB takes it as a spindle, so the curse becomes unmanliness rather than lameness.

records.change: "Is this the manner of man?" becomes "you let a man see this"
records.note: The GNB follows a conjectural reading of an obscure Hebrew phrase (literally "this is the law of man"), which some read as God's charter for humanity through David's line.

records.change: "For thy land" replaced by "you drove out other nations"
records.note: The GNB emends the Masoretic text to match 1 Chronicles 17:21; the KJV follows the Hebrew as it stands.

records.change: "Syria" becomes "Edom"
records.note: The GNB follows the Septuagint, some Hebrew manuscripts and 1 Chronicles 18:11 (Edom); the Masoretic text reads Aram (Syria). The two words differ by one similar letter.

records.change: "Thy master's son" becomes "your master Saul's family"
records.note: The GNB follows some ancient versions ("master's house"); the Masoretic text reads "master's son", meaning Mephibosheth.

records.change: The king's words "at my table" become narration
records.note: The GNB follows the Septuagint ("at David's table") and makes it the narrator's statement; the Masoretic text has David speaking.

records.change: "put them under saws" becomes forced labour with saws and axes
records.note: The Hebrew "put under" / "made pass through" can mean torture or forced labour; the GNB takes the latter, partly by a small emendation.

records.change: Adds "in Hebron" to Absalom's vow
records.note: The words are in some Septuagint manuscripts (Lucianic) but not the Masoretic text; they fit verse 7, where Absalom asks to go to Hebron.

records.change: "the brother of Goliath" becomes "Goliath"
records.note: The Masoretic text lacks "the brother of"; the KJV supplies it in italics from 1 Chronicles 20:5, so the GNB's Elhanan kills Goliath himself, unlike 1 Samuel 17.

records.change: "Horn of my salvation" becomes "he defends me"
records.note: Translation choice that drops the image; the phrase "horn of salvation" is taken up of Christ in Luke 1:69.

records.change: "Sorrows of hell" becomes "the grave"
records.note: Translation choice for Hebrew sheol, which the KJV renders "hell" here and "grave" elsewhere; the Hebrew is the same.

records.change: "The most High" becomes "Almighty God"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew Elyon means "Most High"; "Almighty" usually renders Shaddai. Both are titles of God.

records.change: "His anointed" becomes "the one he has chosen"
records.note: Translation choice that drops "anointed" (Hebrew mashiach), the word behind "Messiah"; the verse promises mercy to David's seed for ever.

records.change: David's doubts ("although my house be not so") become confident statements
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew can be read as statements, as in the KJV, or as rhetorical questions expecting "yes", as in the GNB and most modern versions.

records.change: "Chief among three" becomes leader of "The Thirty"
records.note: The GNB follows the Syriac and two Hebrew manuscripts ("thirty"); the Masoretic text reads "three".

records.change: "Among three mighty men" becomes one of "The Thirty"
records.note: The same choice as verse 18: the GNB reads "thirty" where the Masoretic text reads "three".

records.change: "A young virgin" becomes "a young woman"
records.note: Translation choice: the Hebrew has both na'arah and betulah (virgin); the GNB drops the second word. No textual difference.

records.change: "Captains of the host" becomes "Joab the commander of your army"
records.note: The GNB follows the Septuagint's "Joab the commander"; the Masoretic text reads "the commanders of the army", as in verse 19.

records.change: Blood on Joab's belt becomes David's own guilt and suffering
records.note: The GNB follows the Septuagint ("my belt ... my sandals"); the Masoretic text, followed by the KJV, has Joab's belt and shoes.

records.change: Adds Solomon questioning Joab and Joab's reply
records.note: The added sentences come from the Septuagint; they are not in the Masoretic text followed by the KJV.

records.change: "Seven days and seven days, even fourteen days" becomes seven days
records.note: The GNB follows the Septuagint, which has only one week; the Masoretic text adds a second week (compare 2 Chronicles 7:9).

records.change: Omits "concerning the name of the LORD"
records.note: Translation choice leaving out a hard Hebrew phrase; it ties Solomon's fame to the LORD, which verse 9 still states.

records.change: "sodomites" become "men and women" shrine prostitutes
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew qadesh (masculine), which the GNB takes as cult prostitutes of both sexes.

records.change: "sodomites" become "male and female prostitutes" at pagan shrines
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew qadesh (masculine), which the GNB takes as cult prostitutes of both sexes.

records.change: "Horeb the mount of God" becomes "Sinai, the holy mountain"
records.note: The Hebrew names Horeb; GNB substitutes Sinai, identifying the two as many interpreters do. A translation choice that replaces the text's name with an interpretation.

records.change: "put a lying spirit in the mouth" becomes "made these prophets lie"
records.note: The Masoretic text speaks of a lying spirit; GNB drops the spirit as agent. A translation choice; the spirit still appears in verses 21-22.

records.change: "sodomites" become "male and female prostitutes" at pagan altars
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew qadesh (masculine), which the GNB takes as cult prostitutes of both sexes.

records.change: "double portion of thy spirit" becomes "share of your power"
records.note: The Hebrew is "a double portion of your spirit"; GNB interprets it as power and a successor's share. The reference to spirit is lost; a translation choice.

records.change: "The spirit of Elijah" becomes "The power of Elijah"
records.note: The Hebrew has ruach, spirit; GNB renders it as power. A translation choice that removes the spiritual sense.

records.change: "the ground barren" becomes water "causes miscarriages"
records.note: The Hebrew meshakkelet can mean causing bereavement or miscarriage; KJV applies it to the land, GNB to the people. A translation choice.

records.change: "leprosy" becomes "his disease"
records.note: The Hebrew tsara'at is traditionally leprosy; GNB generalises it to a skin disease. A translation choice; the healing is unchanged.

records.change: "the messenger came" becomes "the king arrived"
records.note: The Masoretic text has "messenger" (mal'ak); GNB follows an emendation to "king" (melek). The speaker of the following words changes.

records.change: "smite the house of Ahab" becomes "kill your master the king"
records.note: The Hebrew commands striking Ahab's whole house; GNB narrows it to King Joram. A translation choice; verses 8-9 still speak of Ahab's family.

records.change: "gave him the testimony" becomes "copy of the laws governing kingship"
records.note: The Hebrew has 'edut, testimony; GNB interprets it as the law of kingship. An interpretive translation choice.

records.change: "put up in bags" becomes "melt down the silver"
records.note: The Hebrew verb tsur may mean to bind up or to cast metal; KJV takes the first, GNB the second. A translation choice.

records.change: "a saviour" becomes "a leader"
records.note: The Hebrew is moshia', deliverer or saviour; GNB uses "leader". A translation choice; the deliverance is still stated.

records.change: "for me to enquire by" becomes "for divination"
records.note: The Hebrew verb baqar means to inquire or consider; GNB interprets Ahaz's use as divination. An interpretive translation choice.

records.change: "covert for the sabbath" becomes "platform for the royal throne"
records.note: The Masoretic text has a sabbath covering; GNB follows the Septuagint's reading of a throne base. A different underlying text.

records.change: "The virgin the daughter of Zion" becomes "The city of Jerusalem"
records.note: The Hebrew personifies Zion as a virgin daughter; GNB drops the figure. A translation choice; no doctrine of virginity is involved.

records.change: Adds Jeroboam standing by the altar at the festival
records.note: The added words are in the Septuagint but not the Masoretic text; GNB follows the Septuagint. It links the event back to 1 Kings 13.

records.change: "would not pardon" becomes "could not forgive"
records.note: The Hebrew lo' 'abah means was not willing; GNB's "could not" suggests inability rather than refusal. A translation choice.

records.change: Makes Ziph father of Mareshah; KJV lists "sons of Mareshah"
records.note: The Hebrew is difficult; GNB rearranges the line as an interpretation (some follow the Septuagint here), where the KJV renders the Masoretic wording directly. A genealogical detail only.

records.change: Makes Hur the son of Caleb, not Caleb son of Hur
records.note: A translation choice in punctuating the Hebrew: GNB and most modern versions read "the son of Hur" as starting a new line, with Hur as Caleb's son by Ephrath (cf. 2:19). The KJV reads Caleb as the son of Hur.

records.change: "came of Hemath, the father of the house of Rechab" becomes intermarriage
records.note: GNB interprets the Hebrew as a relationship by marriage with the Rechabites; the KJV has the Kenites descended from Hemath, ancestor of the Rechabites. A translation choice on a genealogical note.

records.change: "Assir" read as "taken prisoner", not a son's name
records.note: The Hebrew assir means "captive"; GNB takes it as describing Jehoiachin, where the KJV takes it as a son's name. This affects the line to Salathiel (Shealtiel) cited in Matthew 1:12, though Shealtiel remains Jehoiachin's son.

records.change: Hodiah becomes a husband who married, not the wife
records.note: KJV reads "his wife Hodiah the sister of Naham"; GNB makes Hodiah the man who married Naham's sister. A translation choice in a difficult genealogy.

records.change: Pul and Tiglath-pileser made one king
records.note: The Hebrew names both, with a singular verb following; GNB identifies them as one ruler, which matches history but is an interpretation. The KJV reads two kings.

records.change: "firstborn Vashni" replaced by "Joel, the older"
records.note: GNB follows an emendation from 1 Samuel 8:2 (with the Syriac and some Septuagint witnesses), reading Joel and taking "Vashni" as "and the second". The Masoretic text, followed by the KJV, has Vashni.

records.change: Adds the name "Jeiel" as founder of Gibeon
records.note: The name is not in the Masoretic text here; GNB supplies it from 9:35 (as some Septuagint witnesses do). The KJV leaves the father of Gibeon unnamed.

records.change: Adds "Ner" to the list of sons
records.note: Ner is not in the Masoretic text of this verse; GNB adds him from 9:36 and some Septuagint witnesses. The KJV follows the Masoretic list.

records.change: "among the three mighties" becomes one of "The Thirty"
records.note: The Masoretic text has "the three"; GNB adjusts to fit 11:25, where Benaiah was honoured among the thirty but did not attain to the three. An interpretive correction.

records.change: Sacrifice offered to secure God's help, not after it
records.note: KJV reads the sacrifice as following God's help ("when God helped"); GNB makes it a sacrifice "to make sure that God would help". A translation choice on the Hebrew clause.

records.change: "Glory in his holy name" becomes "glad that we belong"
records.note: A free paraphrase of the Hebrew; glorying in God's holy name becomes gladness at belonging to him. The call to praise his name stands in 16:8 and 16:35.

records.change: "beauty of holiness" becomes "the Holy One when he appears"
records.note: A translation choice on hadrat qodesh, read as God's holy appearing rather than holy splendour or attire; "come before him" also becomes "into his Temple". The call to worship remains.

records.change: "went to redeem" becomes "rescued from slavery"
records.note: The Hebrew padah means to redeem or ransom; GNB renders it as rescue. The deliverance from Egypt is still stated, but the vocabulary of redemption is lost.

records.change: "mercy seat" becomes "Most Holy Place, where sins are forgiven"
records.note: A translation choice: GNB explains the kapporet (mercy seat, atonement cover) by its purpose instead of naming it. Forgiveness is kept, but the object Romans 3:25 alludes to is not named.

records.change: "that he had by the spirit" becomes "all he had in mind"
records.note: The Hebrew "in the spirit with him" can mean David's own mind or divine inspiration; the KJV allows the latter, GNB the former. 28:19 still says the plans came from the LORD.

records.change: Drops "priests be clothed with salvation"
records.note: GNB paraphrases the Hebrew as "Bless your priests in all they do", losing the image of priests clothed with salvation (also in Psalm 132:16). A translation choice.

records.change: "glory of the LORD" becomes "the dazzling light"
records.note: A translation choice that renders God's glory as light and drops the divine name. 7:1 and 7:3 still speak of the LORD's presence filling the house.

records.change: "glory of the LORD upon the house" becomes "the light"
records.note: As in 7:2, GNB renders the LORD's glory as light. The people still worship God and praise his goodness.

records.change: "his ascent" into the house becomes "sacrifices he offered"
records.note: GNB follows the parallel in 1 Kings 10:5 and ancient versions (burnt offerings) instead of the Masoretic "his ascent" here, which the KJV follows.

records.change: "set thee on his throne" becomes "making you king"
records.note: The Hebrew says God set Solomon on God's own throne, a theme of Chronicles (1 Chr 29:23); GNB paraphrases it as "to rule in his name". Loses the idea that the throne is the LORD's.

records.change: "prophecy of Oded the prophet" becomes Azariah son of Oded's prophecy
records.note: The Masoretic text reads "of Oded the prophet"; the GNB follows the Syriac and Vulgate, which harmonise with verse 1. A translation choice with no doctrinal effect.

records.change: "praise the beauty of holiness" becomes wearing robes for sacred occasions
records.note: The Hebrew phrase can mean "in holy array"; the GNB takes it as the singers' vestments, where the KJV has them praising God's holiness. A translation choice.

records.change: "Forty and two years old" becomes "twenty-two"
records.note: The Masoretic text has 42; the GNB follows 2 Kings 8:26 and some Septuagint and Syriac witnesses, which have 22.

records.change: "Azariah the son of Jehoram" becomes Ahaziah
records.note: The Masoretic text has Azariah; the GNB follows some Hebrew manuscripts, the Septuagint and 2 Kings 8:29 in reading Ahaziah. Same person either way.

records.change: "the sons of Athaliah" becomes her "followers"
records.note: The Hebrew says "her sons"; the GNB takes it as her supporters, since her sons were killed earlier (22:1). A translation choice.

records.change: "the sons of Jehoiada" becomes the son (singular)
records.note: The Masoretic text has the plural; the GNB follows the Septuagint and Vulgate, matching the one son, Zechariah, killed in verses 20-22.

records.change: "if thou wilt go… be strong" becomes "you may think they will make you stronger"
records.note: The GNB follows a common emendation of an obscure Masoretic sentence. The point that God gives victory or defeat stays in both.

records.change: Zechariah "had understanding in the visions of God" becomes "religious adviser"
records.note: The Masoretic text speaks of understanding visions of God (some manuscripts and the Septuagint read "fear of God"); the GNB generalises it and loses the prophetic sense.

records.change: "first year of his reign" becomes the year after he became king
records.note: The Hebrew says the first year of his reign; the GNB interprets it as the first full year after his accession. A translation choice about dating.

records.change: "not done it of a long time" becomes "in larger numbers than ever"
records.note: The Hebrew word can mean "in great numbers" or "for a long time"; the GNB takes the first. The KJV's point that Passover had long been neglected is lost.

records.change: "from three years old" becomes "thirty years of age"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads three; the GNB follows an emendation to thirty, the age of Levitical service. A textual choice.

records.change: Omits "for ever" from God's putting his name there
records.note: The Masoretic text has "for ever"; the GNB text here leaves it out. The same promise with "forever" stands in verse 4.

records.change: Omits "And so did they with the oxen"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text; the GNB text here ends without it. No doctrine is affected.

records.change: "eight years old" becomes "eighteen"
records.note: Most Hebrew manuscripts have eight; the GNB follows 2 Kings 24:8, some Hebrew manuscripts and the Septuagint, which have eighteen.

records.change: "Zedekiah his brother" becomes Jehoiachin's "uncle"
records.note: The Hebrew says brother (or kinsman); the GNB follows 2 Kings 24:17, where Zedekiah is Jehoiachin's uncle. A harmonising translation choice.

records.change: "the sons of Judah" becomes "the clan of Hodaviah"
records.note: The Masoretic text reads "sons of Judah" (Yehudah); the GNB emends it to Hodaviah to match Ezra 2:40. A textual choice about a Levite clan.

records.change: "let the foundations be strongly laid" becomes where "offerings are burned"
records.note: The GNB follows an emendation of one Aramaic word ("its foundations" read as "its fire offerings"), as the RSV does. No doctrinal effect.

records.change: "the work of their Lord" becomes work set "by the supervisors"
records.note: The Hebrew can mean "their lord" or "their masters"; the KJV reads it as God, the GNB as human overseers. A translation choice.

records.change: "thy good spirit to instruct them" becomes "in your goodness you told them"
records.note: The Masoretic text has "your good Spirit"; the GNB paraphrase drops the Spirit as the one who instructs. The Spirit's work in the prophets remains implied in verse 30.

records.change: "by thy spirit in thy prophets" becomes "you inspired your prophets"
records.note: The Hebrew names God's Spirit as speaking through the prophets; the GNB keeps the idea of inspiration but not the Spirit by name. A translation choice.

records.change: Makes Ahitub, not Seraiah, the ruler of God's house
records.note: Hebrew allows either referent for "ruler of the house of God"; GNB chooses Ahitub and calls him High Priest, a translation choice.

records.change: "Johanan the son" becomes "Jonathan, the grandson" of Eliashib
records.note: GNB harmonises the name and relation with 12:10-11; the Masoretic text here reads Johanan, and "son" can mean descendant.

records.change: Adds Binnui; "Jeshua son of Kadmiel" becomes three names
records.note: GNB emends Hebrew ben ("son of") to the name Binnui, as in 12:8 and 10:9; the Masoretic text reads "son of Kadmiel".

records.change: Joiada expelled rather than his son who married Sanballat's daughter
records.note: In the Hebrew and KJV it is the son-in-law of Sanballat whom Nehemiah drives away; GNB applies it to Joiada, a translation choice.

records.change: "Sons of God" becomes "heavenly beings"
records.note: "Sons of God" (bene elohim) is rendered by its usual interpretation; a translation choice, but the KJV's literal title is not kept.

records.change: "Fire of God fallen from heaven" becomes "Lightning"
records.note: Translation choice interpreting the Hebrew idiom; the text no longer names God as the source of the fire.

records.change: "Sons of God" becomes "heavenly beings"
records.note: "Sons of God" (bene elohim) is rendered by its usual interpretation; a translation choice, but the KJV's literal title is not kept.

records.change: "A spirit" becomes "a light breeze"
records.note: Hebrew ruach can mean spirit or wind; GNB chooses wind, so the vision of a spirit passing by is lost.

records.change: Drops "perish for ever"
records.note: Hebrew lanetsach (for ever) is rendered only by dying unnoticed; a translation choice that loses the permanence of the ruin.

records.change: "I have sinned" becomes a question; "preserver of men" becomes "jailer"
records.note: The Hebrew can be read as a conditional ("if I have sinned"); "watcher of men" is taken negatively by the GNB, and "burden to you" follows an ancient scribal tradition over the KJV's "to myself".

records.change: "Deeper than hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: Hebrew Sheol, which the KJV renders "hell", is translated "world of the dead"; a translation choice that removes the sense of punishment the KJV's word carries. GNB also makes God, not his wisdom, the subject.

records.change: God enriching them becomes "their only god is their strength"
records.note: The Hebrew clause is obscure; GNB follows an interpretation like Habakkuk 1:11 rather than the KJV's reading that God enriches them.

records.change: "He shall be my salvation" becomes "my boldness will save me"
records.note: Hebrew gam-hu can mean "he" or "this"; GNB takes it as Job's boldness, so God is no longer named as Job's salvation.

records.change: "my redeemer liveth" becomes "someone in heaven"; "stand upon the earth" dropped
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew go'el; the KJV's redeemer standing on the earth at the last day is widely read of Christ and the resurrection, and the GNB makes it an unnamed defender.

records.change: After-death seeing of God becomes "while still in this body"
records.note: Hebrew mibbesari can mean "from" or "apart from" my flesh; GNB reads disease in life, losing the KJV's sense of seeing God after death, often read of resurrection.

records.change: "Perish for ever" becomes "blown away like dust"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew lanetsach (for ever) is not rendered, so the permanence of the ruin is lost.

records.change: "Hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: Hebrew Sheol, which the KJV renders "hell", is translated "world of the dead"; a translation choice that removes the sense of punishment the KJV's word carries.

records.change: "By his spirit" becomes "his breath"; serpent becomes monster
records.note: Hebrew ruach can mean spirit, wind or breath; GNB's choice loses the KJV's reference to God's Spirit in creation.

records.change: "God shall cast upon him" becomes the wind blowing
records.note: The Hebrew subject is unstated; GNB takes it as the east wind of verse 21, the KJV supplies God.

records.change: "Chosen iniquity rather than affliction" becomes suffering sent to prevent evil
records.note: Translation choice on an obscure clause; the KJV rebukes Job for preferring sin, GNB says suffering guards him from it.

records.change: "Sons of God" becomes "heavenly beings"
records.note: "Sons of God" (bene elohim) is rendered by its usual interpretation; a translation choice, but the KJV's literal title is not kept.

records.change: "Who hath prevented me" becomes "Who can attack him"
records.note: GNB follows the Septuagint's "him" (Leviathan) for Hebrew "me"; the KJV's claim that all under heaven is God's is lost.

records.change: "My Son... begotten thee" becomes "my son... become your father"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew yelidtikha is "I have begotten you", and the verse is applied to Christ in Acts 13:33 and Hebrews 1:5, where the KJV's wording is kept.

records.change: "Kiss the Son" omitted; becomes "bow down to him"
records.note: GNB emends the Hebrew nashqu-bar with verse 11; the Masoretic text reads "kiss the son", a messianic reading the KJV keeps.

records.change: Omits superscription about David fleeing Absalom
records.note: The superscription is part of the Masoretic text, where the KJV numbers it with verse 1; this GNB text leaves it out of the verse, so the psalm's attribution and occasion are not shown here.

records.change: "Salvation belongeth unto the LORD" becomes "Victory comes from the LORD"
records.note: Hebrew yeshuah means deliverance or victory; a translation choice that narrows the KJV's broader word "salvation".

records.change: Omits superscription about Cush the Benjamite
records.note: The superscription is part of the Masoretic text, where the KJV numbers it with verse 1; this GNB text leaves it out of the verse, so the psalm's attribution and occasion are not shown here.

records.change: "The son of man" becomes "mere mortals"
records.note: Translation choice; Hebrews 2:6-9 applies the verse to Christ, and the KJV's title "son of man" is not kept.

records.change: "a little lower than the angels" becomes "inferior only to yourself"
records.note: The Hebrew has elohim; the KJV follows the Septuagint's "angels", as Hebrews 2:7 quotes it. The GNB's plural "them" also loses the reading Hebrews 2:9 applies to Jesus.

records.change: "Turned into hell" becomes "Death is the destiny"
records.note: Hebrew Sheol, which the KJV renders "hell", is translated "world of the dead"; a translation choice that removes the sense of punishment the KJV's word carries.

records.change: "Keep them" becomes "Keep us"
records.note: GNB follows some Hebrew manuscripts and the Septuagint; the Masoretic text reads "them", the poor of verse 5.

records.change: "Salvation of Israel" becomes "victory"
records.note: Translation choice for Hebrew yeshuah; the KJV's "salvation" out of Zion, often read messianically, is narrowed.

records.change: "Thine Holy One" and "see corruption" lost
records.note: Translation choice; Hebrew chasid and shachat (corruption, pit) are rendered generally, though Acts 2:27 and 13:35 quote this of Christ's resurrection.

records.change: God's "hid treasure" becomes stored-up sufferings for punishment
records.note: Translation choice on a hard Hebrew verse; the KJV describes worldly men God fills with good things, GNB a prayer for their punishment.

records.change: Omits superscription about deliverance from Saul
records.note: The superscription is part of the Masoretic text, where the KJV numbers it with verse 1; this GNB text leaves it out of the verse, so the psalm's attribution and occasion are not shown here.

records.change: "Sorrows of hell" becomes "danger of death"
records.note: Hebrew Sheol, which the KJV renders "hell", is translated "world of the dead"; a translation choice that removes the sense of punishment the KJV's word carries.

records.change: "where their voice is not heard" becomes "no sound is heard"
records.note: The Hebrew is terse; the KJV reads it as the heavens heard everywhere, the GNB as a wordless witness, reversing the sense.

records.change: Omits superscription "A Psalm of David"
records.note: The superscription is part of the Masoretic text, where the KJV numbers it with verse 1; this GNB text leaves it out of the verse, so the psalm's attribution and occasion are not shown here.

records.change: "They pierced my hands and my feet" becomes "tear at"
records.note: Most Masoretic manuscripts read ka'ari ("like a lion"); the Septuagint and a Dead Sea Psalms scroll support "pierced", which the KJV follows, a reading of the crucifixion.

records.change: Drops "eat and worship" and "none can keep alive his soul"
records.note: GNB follows an emended Hebrew text ("all who sleep in the earth"); the Masoretic text reads as the KJV.

records.change: "For ever" becomes "as long as I live"
records.note: Hebrew le'orekh yamim is literally "for length of days"; GNB is literal where the KJV reads "for ever", so eternal dwelling is not stated.

records.change: "King of glory" becomes "the great king"
records.note: Translation choice; the title of God, repeated in verses 8-10, is dropped here.

records.change: "King of glory" becomes "the great king"
records.note: Translation choice; the title of God, repeated in verses 8-10, is dropped here.

records.change: Omits superscription "A Psalm of David"
records.note: The superscription is part of the Masoretic text, where the KJV numbers it with verse 1; this GNB text leaves it out of the verse, so the psalm's attribution and occasion are not shown here.

records.change: Omits superscription; "ye mighty" becomes "heavenly beings"
records.note: The superscription is part of the Masoretic text, where the KJV numbers it with verse 1; this GNB text leaves it out of the verse, so the psalm's attribution and occasion are not shown here. Hebrew bene elim is interpreted as heavenly beings.

records.change: "In the beauty of holiness" becomes "when he appears"
records.note: Translation choice; the Hebrew hadrat-qodesh (holy splendour or attire) is read as God's appearing.

records.change: "Into thine hand I commit my spirit" becomes "I place myself"
records.note: Translation choice; Jesus quotes these words at his death in Luke 23:46, and "redeemed" becomes "save".

records.change: "I have hated" becomes "You hate"
records.note: GNB follows the Septuagint, Syriac and one Hebrew manuscript; the Masoretic text reads "I have hated".

records.change: Omits superscription; "my heart" becomes "their hearts"
records.note: The superscription is part of the Masoretic text, where the KJV numbers it with verse 1; this GNB text leaves it out of the verse, so the psalm's attribution and occasion are not shown here. GNB also follows manuscripts reading "his heart".

records.change: "Grace is poured into thy lips" becomes "eloquent speaker"
records.note: Translation choice in a psalm Hebrews 1:8-9 applies to Christ; "therefore God hath blessed thee" also loses its cause.

records.change: "He is thy Lord; worship thou him" becomes "master... obey him"
records.note: Translation choice; Hebrew adon and hishtachavi allow "lord" and "bow down", but the KJV's worship of the king, read messianically, is lost.

records.change: Omits "for he shall receive me"
records.note: The Hebrew has "he will take me", read by many as hope of being received beyond death; the GNB folds it into being saved from death.

records.change: "in sin did my mother conceive me" becomes "I have been sinful"
records.note: A translation choice; the Hebrew speaks of being brought forth in iniquity and conceived in sin. The GNB keeps sinfulness from conception but moves the focus from the mother's act.

records.change: "Bloodguiltiness" becomes "Spare my life"
records.note: Hebrew damim (bloodshed) is read as danger to the psalmist's life rather than guilt for shedding blood.

records.change: "The sacrifices of God" becomes "My sacrifice"
records.note: GNB follows an emendation of the Hebrew zivchei elohim; the Masoretic text reads as the KJV.

records.change: "Quick into hell" becomes "alive into the world of the dead"
records.note: Hebrew Sheol, which the KJV renders "hell", is translated "world of the dead"; a translation choice that removes the sense of punishment the KJV's word carries.

records.change: "Abide in thy tabernacle for ever" becomes "all my life"
records.note: Hebrew olamim means for ages; GNB narrows it to a lifetime, so eternal dwelling is not stated.

records.change: Omits superscription to Jeduthun, a Psalm of David
records.note: The superscription is part of the Masoretic text, where the KJV numbers it with verse 1; this GNB text leaves it out of the verse, so the psalm's attribution and occasion are not shown here.

records.change: "the company of those that published it" becomes "many women"
records.note: The Hebrew participle is feminine; the KJV renders it generally, the GNB specifies women.

records.change: Drops "thousands of angels"; the Lord comes from Sinai
records.note: GNB follows an emended Hebrew text (ba missinai); the Masoretic text reads "as in Sinai".

records.change: Omits "the king's son"
records.note: A translation choice that merges the parallel lines into one king. The KJV keeps the royal son of this psalm, which Christian readers take as messianic.

records.change: "men shall be blessed in him" becomes nations asking blessing like his
records.note: A translation choice taking the Hebrew verb as reflexive, as GNB does in Genesis 26:4. The KJV makes the king the source of blessing for all nations, echoing the promise to Abraham.

records.change: "the son of man" becomes "the people you have chosen"
records.note: A translation choice reading the singular Hebrew "man of thy right hand" and "son of man" as the nation Israel. The KJV keeps one individual, read by the Targum and Christian interpreters as the Messiah.

records.change: "their time should have endured" becomes "their punishment would last"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew "their time". The KJV can be read of Israel's lasting prosperity; GNB makes it the enemies' lasting punishment.

records.change: "the lowest hell" becomes "the grave itself"
records.note: A translation choice for Hebrew Sheol, which the KJV renders "hell" here. GNB makes it the grave rather than a place below.

records.change: "thy holy one" becomes plural "your faithful servants"
records.note: Hebrew manuscripts differ between singular and plural here; the KJV follows the singular, GNB the plural of the printed Masoretic text. Not doctrinal.

records.change: "destroyed for ever" becomes "totally destroyed"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew "unto perpetuity". The KJV states the wicked's destruction is for ever; GNB keeps only its completeness.

records.change: "in the beauty of holiness" becomes "when he appears"
records.note: A translation choice for an uncertain Hebrew phrase, read as holy attire or a holy appearing. GNB moves the holiness from the worshippers to God's appearing.

records.change: Command "worship him, all ye gods" becomes a statement
records.note: The Hebrew form can be imperative or perfect; the KJV takes the command, which Hebrews 1:6 echoes through the Septuagint. GNB says the gods do bow.

records.change: "cometh to judge the earth" becomes "comes to rule"
records.note: The Hebrew verb means both judge and rule; GNB takes rule. The KJV's coming judgment of the world is softened to governing.

records.change: "Thou sendest forth thy spirit" becomes "you give them breath"
records.note: A translation choice for Hebrew ruach, which means both spirit and breath. The KJV ascribes creation to God's Spirit; GNB reads it as the breath of life.

records.change: "they rebelled not" becomes "the Egyptians did not obey"
records.note: The Masoretic text has the negative (Moses and Aaron did not rebel); the GNB follows the Septuagint and Syriac, which lack "not", and makes the Egyptians the subject.

records.change: "fasting" becomes "lack of food"
records.note: The Hebrew word is the usual one for a religious fast. GNB makes it simple hunger, losing the psalmist's fasting.

records.change: "the pains of hell" becomes "the horrors of the grave"
records.note: A translation choice for Hebrew Sheol, which the KJV renders "hell" here. GNB makes it the grave.

records.change: "the cup of salvation" becomes "a wine offering"
records.note: A translation choice interpreting the cup as a drink offering of thanks. The KJV keeps the image of a cup of salvation taken from God.

records.change: "clothe her priests with salvation" becomes "bless her priests"
records.note: A translation choice reading the Hebrew "salvation" as prosperity. The KJV's priests clothed with salvation become priests who succeed.

records.change: "magnified thy word above all thy name" becomes name and commands supreme
records.note: The Hebrew is difficult; GNB rephrases it, as many modern versions do, so that name and word stand together. The KJV's word exalted above God's name is lost.

records.change: "from thy spirit" becomes "from you"
records.note: A translation choice treating God's Spirit as God himself, in parallel with "presence". The KJV names the Spirit, a text often cited for the Spirit's omnipresence.

records.change: "make my bed in hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: A translation choice for Hebrew Sheol, which the KJV renders "hell" here. GNB makes it the realm of the dead.

records.change: Omits "thy spirit is good"; becomes "Be good to me"
records.note: A translation choice; the Masoretic text has "thy spirit is good, let it lead me". GNB drops God's Spirit as the one who leads.

records.change: "I will pour out my spirit" becomes "give you good advice"
records.note: A translation choice taking wisdom's "spirit" as her counsel. The KJV keeps the image of a spirit poured out, which some read alongside Joel 2:28.

records.change: "hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: A translation choice for Hebrew Sheol, which the KJV renders "hell" here and "grave" elsewhere. GNB makes it the realm of the dead rather than a place of punishment.

records.change: "the way to hell" becomes way "to the world of the dead"
records.note: As in 5:5, a translation choice for Sheol.

records.change: "The LORD possessed me" becomes "The LORD created me"
records.note: Hebrew qanah can mean possess, acquire or create; GNB follows the Septuagint's "created". Christian readers who take Wisdom here as the eternal Son read "possessed"; "created" was the Arian proof text.

records.change: "set up from everlasting" becomes "made in the very beginning"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew says Wisdom was installed from everlasting. GNB's "made" and loss of "everlasting" follow its reading of 8:22 and weaken Wisdom's eternity.

records.change: "the depths of hell" becomes "deep in the world of the dead"
records.note: As in 5:5, a translation choice for Sheol.

records.change: "Hell and destruction" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: A translation choice for Sheol and Abaddon; GNB also merges the two into one. The KJV names two places open before the LORD.

records.change: "depart from hell beneath" becomes the road "downward to death"
records.note: As in 5:5, a translation choice for Sheol; GNB makes it death itself.

records.change: "must shew himself friendly" becomes "Some friendships do not last"
records.note: The Hebrew of the first line is obscure; the KJV follows one reading of the verb, the GNB another ("come to ruin").

records.change: "deliver his soul from hell" becomes "save their lives"
records.note: A translation choice for Sheol, read as early death. The KJV's reading speaks of the soul's deliverance.

records.change: "The great God that formed all things" becomes "An employer"
records.note: The Hebrew is obscure: rab can mean the Great One, a master or an archer. The KJV reads it as God rewarding all; GNB as a man hiring fools.

records.change: "Hell and destruction" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: As in 15:11, a translation choice for Sheol and Abaddon.

records.change: "the people perish" becomes "a nation without order"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew verb means to be let loose or unrestrained; "vision" is also made "God's guidance".

records.change: Servant becoming "his son" becomes servants taking "everything you own"
records.note: The Hebrew word at the end (manon) occurs only here and is uncertain. The KJV guesses "son", GNB something like heir or ruin. Not doctrinal.

records.change: Names "Ithiel" and "Ucal" become "God is not with me… helpless"
records.note: The GNB revocalizes the Masoretic names into a sentence; the KJV keeps them as persons addressed.

records.change: "his name... his son's name" becomes "Who are they... their children?"
records.note: A translation choice making the Masoretic singulars plural. The KJV asks after one Creator and his Son, a verse Christians read of Christ (compare John 3:13); GNB makes it about human sages.

records.change: King "the son of nobles" becomes one who "makes his own decisions"
records.note: A translation choice reading the Hebrew idiom as free-born, independent character rather than noble birth. Not doctrinal.

records.change: "the spirit shall return unto God" becomes "the breath of life"
records.note: Hebrew ruach means both spirit and breath; GNB takes the second. The KJV reading is often cited for the survival of the human spirit after death.

records.change: "hell hath enlarged herself" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: A translation choice for Hebrew Sheol, which the KJV renders "hell" here. GNB makes it the realm of the dead rather than a place of punishment.

records.change: "a virgin shall conceive" becomes "a young woman who is pregnant"
records.note: A translation choice for Hebrew almah; the Septuagint has parthenos, "virgin", which Matthew 1:23 quotes of Christ's birth. GNB's "is pregnant" also makes the conception already past.

records.change: "should not a people seek unto their God?" becomes the mediums' advice
records.note: A translation choice: Hebrew elohim can mean God or spirits, and GNB reads the question as the mediums' claim that people should consult spirits. The KJV makes it the prophet's rebuke.

records.change: "not increased the joy" becomes "You have given them great joy"
records.note: GNB follows the Masoretic marginal reading (qere, "to it") and a common emendation; the KJV follows the written text (ketiv, "not").

records.change: Sixfold "spirit of" list merged; "counsel and might" lost
records.note: A paraphrase of the Masoretic text. The KJV names the Spirit's gifts resting on the Messiah one by one; GNB keeps wisdom and knowledge but drops might and counsel.

records.change: Omits "every one joined unto them shall fall by the sword"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text; the GNB compresses the parallel lines into one, losing the second.

records.change: "Hell from beneath" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: As in 5:14, a translation choice for Sheol.

records.change: "O Lucifer, son of the morning" becomes "King of Babylon, morning star"
records.note: Hebrew helel means shining one; the KJV follows the Vulgate's name Lucifer, long read of Satan's fall. GNB supplies "King of Babylon" from 14:4 and uses a title Revelation 22:16 gives Christ.

records.change: "mount of the congregation" becomes mountain "where the gods assemble"
records.note: A translation choice reading the phrase against Canaanite myth; GNB also drops "of God" from "stars of God".

records.change: "brought down to hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: As in 5:14, a translation choice for Sheol.

records.change: "the firstborn of the poor shall feed" becomes the LORD a shepherd
records.note: GNB follows an emendation of the Hebrew ("in my pastures" for "firstborn") where the KJV keeps the Masoretic text. Not doctrinal.

records.change: "sluices and ponds for fish" becomes "weavers and skilled workers"
records.note: The Hebrew is obscure; the GNB revocalizes it, the KJV follows another reading.

records.change: "a saviour, and a great one" becomes "someone to rescue them"
records.note: A translation choice; GNB drops "a great one" (or "a champion"). Some read the promised saviour of Egypt messianically.

records.change: "he cried, A lion" becomes "The sentry calls out"
records.note: GNB follows the Dead Sea Isaiah scroll ("the watcher"), where the KJV keeps the Masoretic "lion". Not doctrinal.

records.change: "glorify ye the LORD in the fires" becomes "those in the East"
records.note: A translation choice for the obscure Hebrew urim (lights, fires), read as the region of sunrise. Not doctrinal.

records.change: "with hell are we at agreement" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: A translation choice for Hebrew Sheol, which the KJV renders "hell" here. GNB makes it the realm of the dead rather than a place of punishment.

records.change: "tried stone... he that believeth" becomes an inscribed cornerstone motto
records.note: A translation choice reading the believer clause as words written on the stone and dropping "tried". Romans 9:33 and 1 Peter 2:6 quote the verse of Christ and of faith in him; GNB's wording loses that.

records.change: "agreement with hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: As in 28:15, a translation choice for Sheol.

records.change: "satyr" and "screech owl" become "demons" and "night monster"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew se'irim and lilith; the GNB takes them as spirit beings, the KJV as creatures.

records.change: "his reward is with him" becomes "the people he has rescued"
records.note: A translation choice reading the reward as the redeemed people he brings. The KJV's wording is echoed in Revelation 22:12 of Christ's coming.

records.change: "the Spirit of the LORD" becomes "the LORD"
records.note: The Masoretic text has ruach YHWH; GNB drops the Spirit. Paul quotes the verse from the Septuagint as "the mind of the Lord" (Romans 11:34).

records.change: Omits "blind as he that is perfect... the LORD's servant"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text; GNB drops it as repetition of the first half. Christian readers apply the servant's titles here to Israel, not the Messiah.

records.change: "create evil" becomes "bring disaster"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew ra', which can mean calamity or moral evil; the verse is often debated on God and evil.

records.change: "righteousness" and "salvation" become "victory" and "freedom"
records.note: A translation choice: GNB renders Hebrew tsedeq and yesha in these chapters as political victory and liberation. The KJV keeps the moral and spiritual words.

records.change: Omits "even to him shall men come"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text; GNB leaves it out in its paraphrase. The nations' coming to the LORD is still stated in 45:14 and 45:22.

records.change: "I have chosen thee" becomes "found that you are worthless"
records.note: GNB reads "tested" with the Dead Sea Isaiah Scroll (and Aramaic usage) and makes the refining find no silver. The KJV follows the Masoretic "chosen", a word of election.

records.change: "the Lord GOD, and his Spirit" becomes "given me his power"
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew names the Spirit as sending with the Lord GOD, a verse long read of Father, Son and Spirit. GNB makes the Spirit the LORD's power.

records.change: "Though Israel be not gathered" becomes "bring back ... Israel"
records.note: GNB follows the Masoretic marginal reading (qere) "to him"; the KJV follows the written text (ketiv) "not", so that the servant is honoured even if Israel refuses.

records.change: Spoken "to his people", not the servant made a covenant
records.note: A translation choice: the KJV's "thee" continues the servant of 49:1-7, given "for a covenant of the people" as in 42:6. GNB addresses Israel and makes the covenant come through them.

records.change: "the land of Sinim" becomes "Aswan in the south"
records.note: The Masoretic text has Sinim; the GNB follows the Dead Sea Isaiah Scroll's "Syene" (Aswan).

records.change: "my righteous servant justify many" becomes "I will forgive them"
records.note: GNB follows the Dead Sea Scroll and Septuagint in part ("he will see light", rendered "again have joy") and rewords the Hebrew "make righteous" as God forgiving. His bearing their iniquities is kept.

records.change: "everlasting covenant" becomes "lasting covenant"
records.note: A translation choice for Hebrew 'olam, which the KJV renders "everlasting". "Lasting" is weaker than for ever; the promise to David is kept.

records.change: "the king" becomes "Molech"; "hell" becomes "world of the dead"
records.note: GNB revocalises melek as the god Molech, and renders Sheol as the realm of the dead where the KJV has "hell". Both are translation choices on the Masoretic text.

records.change: Omits "I create the fruit of the lips"
records.note: The clause is in the Masoretic text; GNB leaves it out. It makes God the author of the praise and peace that follow.

records.change: "the Spirit of the LORD shall lift up a standard" gone
records.note: A different parsing of the Hebrew: GNB makes the LORD come like a river driven by a strong wind (ruach). The KJV reads the enemy coming like a flood and the Spirit of the LORD resisting him.

records.change: "My spirit that is upon thee" becomes "my power"
records.note: A translation choice rendering ruach as power. The KJV names God's Spirit given with his words to the people for ever.

records.change: "the LORD hath anointed me" becomes "He has chosen me"
records.note: A translation choice: Hebrew mashach, from which "Messiah" comes, and which Jesus read of himself in Luke 4:18. GNB keeps the Spirit but loses the anointing.

records.change: "his reward is with him" becomes "people he has rescued"
records.note: A translation choice: GNB reads the reward and work as the redeemed he brings. The KJV's "thy salvation cometh ... his reward is with him" is echoed of Christ in Revelation 22:12.

records.change: "the Spirit of the LORD caused him to rest" becomes "the LORD"
records.note: The Masoretic text names the Spirit of the LORD; GNB gives the act to the LORD. The Holy Spirit is still named in 63:10-11.

records.change: Sacrifice likened to murder becomes people doing both alike
records.note: A translation choice on terse Hebrew. The KJV says their sacrifice is as hateful as killing a man; GNB says they sacrifice and kill people indiscriminately.

records.change: Adds that dishonest scribes have changed the laws
records.note: A translation choice: the Hebrew "the lying pen of the scribes" may mean falsifying or false teaching. The KJV says the law was made in vain for them.

records.change: "I will surely consume them" becomes "I wanted to gather"
records.note: The Hebrew root can mean gather or sweep away; GNB takes it as a harvest and renders the obscure last clause as outsiders taking the land. The KJV reads it as judgment.

records.change: "THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS" becomes "The LORD Our Salvation"
records.note: The Hebrew is YHWH tsidqenu, "righteousness"; the GNB renders the sense as salvation, losing the title read of Christ as the believer's righteousness.

records.change: "Jehoiakim" becomes "Zedekiah"
records.note: Most Hebrew manuscripts have Jehoiakim; the GNB follows a few Hebrew manuscripts and the Syriac, matching verses 3 and 12. The Septuagint lacks the verse.

records.change: "The LORD hath appeared ... unto me" becomes "I appeared to them"
records.note: The Masoretic text has "to me"; GNB follows the Septuagint's "to him" and takes the speaker as God throughout. The everlasting love of the verse is kept.

records.change: "A woman shall compass a man" made a simile of protection
records.note: A translation choice on an obscure Hebrew line that some older interpreters read of the virgin birth; GNB renders it as an image of reversal, so that reading is lost.

records.change: "Not yet gone back" becomes "When I did not answer"
records.note: The Masoretic phrase is obscure; GNB follows an interpretation or emendation of it rather than the KJV's literal rendering. The narrative sense is otherwise unchanged.

records.change: "I repent me of the evil" becomes "has caused me great sorrow"
records.note: A translation choice for the Hebrew nacham: KJV reads God relenting of the judgment, GNB reads God grieving over it.

records.change: "Ye dissembled in your hearts" becomes "you are making a fatal mistake"
records.note: A translation choice on the Hebrew verb (you erred, or misled yourselves): KJV charges the people with deceit, GNB with a deadly error.

records.change: Desert beasts and owls become "demons and evil spirits"
records.note: A translation choice for creatures the Hebrew names obscurely; the KJV reads animals, GNB spirit beings. Babylon's desolation is stated in both.

records.change: Omits "whither the spirit was to go" guiding the creatures
records.note: A paraphrase choice: the Hebrew says the creatures went where the spirit was to go; GNB says they went wherever they wished, losing the spirit's direction.

records.change: "Neither have done according to" the nations becomes "have followed" their customs
records.note: The Masoretic text has "not"; GNB follows Hebrew manuscripts and the Syriac without it, as in Ezekiel 11:12. The charge of disobedience to God's laws stands in both.

records.change: "The glory of the God of Israel" becomes "the dazzling light"
records.note: A translation choice: GNB renders kabod as a visible light and drops the divine name here. God's glory in the temple vision is still named elsewhere in Ezekiel.

records.change: "One heart" becomes "a new heart"; "new spirit" becomes "new mind"
records.note: "One heart" is the Masoretic reading; "new" follows some Hebrew manuscripts and the Syriac, with the Septuagint reading "another heart". The promised inner renewal is kept, but the spirit becomes a mind.

records.change: "The glory of the LORD" becomes "the dazzling light"
records.note: A translation choice: GNB renders God's glory as light and omits "the LORD". The departure of God's presence from the city is still described.

records.change: "Daniel" becomes "Danel"
records.note: The consonantal Hebrew (kethiv) reads dn'l, which GNB takes as the ancient figure Danel rather than the prophet Daniel. The Masoretic vowels and the KJV read Daniel.

records.change: "Daniel" becomes "Danel"
records.note: As in 14:14, GNB follows the consonantal spelling dn'l and a different identification of the righteous man. The Masoretic vowels read Daniel.

records.change: Omits "How weak is thine heart"
records.note: The Hebrew phrase is obscure and GNB leaves it out rather than translate it. The accusation of shameless harlotry is kept.

records.change: Omits "in thy blood"
records.note: The Masoretic "in thy blood" is hard to explain and is often emended (e.g. to "in a vineyard"); GNB drops it. The vine image is otherwise kept.

records.change: "It contemneth the rod of my son" becomes disregarding warnings
records.note: The Hebrew is obscure; GNB interprets it as Israel ignoring discipline. Some read "rod of my son" as the royal sceptre of Judah (Genesis 49:10), which GNB loses.

records.change: "If the sword contemn even the rod" becomes "refuse to repent"
records.note: A paraphrase of an obscure Hebrew verse; GNB supplies repentance, which the KJV's text does not mention, and drops the sceptre ("rod") image.

records.change: Omits "and Seir"
records.note: GNB follows the Septuagint, which lacks "and Seir"; the Masoretic text has Moab and Seir. Edom (Seir) is judged separately in 25:12-14.

records.change: "Thou art the anointed cherub" becomes an angel guarding him
records.note: GNB follows the Septuagint ("with the cherub I placed you") rather than the Masoretic "thou art the cherub". The king is no longer himself the cherub, which bears on readings of this passage about Satan.

records.change: "Destroy thee, O covering cherub" becomes the angel driving him away
records.note: Follows the Septuagint here too: the cherub expels the king instead of being the king addressed. The king's expulsion from God's mountain is kept.

records.change: "Hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: Hebrew sheol, the realm of the dead; a translation choice. The KJV's "hell" carries a sense of punishment that GNB's wording does not.

records.change: "Hell" becomes "the world of the dead"; "his arm" reworded
records.note: Sheol rendered as the realm of the dead, a translation choice. "They that were his arm" (his allies) becomes those scattered among the nations, a paraphrase of obscure Hebrew.

records.change: "Hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: Sheol rendered as the realm of the dead, a translation choice; the fall of the uncircumcised slain is kept.

records.change: "Hell" becomes "the world of the dead"; "iniquities" become "shields"
records.note: Sheol is rendered as the realm of the dead. "Shields" follows a common emendation of the Masoretic "their iniquities shall be upon their bones", dropping the statement of guilt.

records.change: "My servant David" becomes "a king like my servant David"
records.note: The Hebrew names "my servant David" as prince; GNB makes it a king like him. The messianic reading, a coming David, is softened; 34:23 and 37:24-25 carry the same promise.

records.change: Omits "I the LORD their God am with them"
records.note: GNB paraphrases God's presence as "I protect Israel" and drops the divine name and title. The covenant formula "they are my people" is kept.

records.change: "cause thy nations to fall" becomes "rob the nation of its children"
records.note: The GNB follows the written Hebrew (ketiv, "bereave"), matching verses 13-14; the KJV follows the marginal reading (qere, "cause to stumble").

records.change: "a new spirit" becomes "a new mind"; "heart of flesh" "obedient heart"
records.note: A translation choice for Hebrew ruach and basar; the image of an inward spiritual renewal is flattened. Verse 27 still promises God's own spirit.

records.change: "my spirit in you" becomes "my breath in them"
records.note: Hebrew ruach can mean spirit or breath; the GNB carries on the breath image of verses 5-10, where the KJV reads God's Spirit giving life.

records.change: Omits "with all the young lions thereof"
records.note: The GNB reads the Hebrew kephirim (young lions) as "villages" or "towns", a revocalization; the KJV keeps the lions as a figure for rulers.

records.change: "shalt thou not know it?" becomes "you will set out"
records.note: The GNB follows the Septuagint ("wilt thou not rouse thyself") instead of the Masoretic "know" that the KJV keeps.

records.change: "call for a sword against him" becomes "terrify Gog with calamities"
records.note: The GNB follows the Septuagint's "every terror"; the Masoretic text, with the KJV, has a sword called over God's mountains.

records.change: "bring again the captivity of Jacob" becomes "make them prosperous again"
records.note: Hebrew shuv shevut can mean return from captivity or restore fortunes; the GNB takes the latter, so the return from exile is not stated.

records.change: Omits "in their high places" for the kings' corpses
records.note: The GNB reads the Hebrew bamotam as "at their death" (a different vowel reading); the KJV's reference to idolatrous high places is lost.

records.change: "troubled to know the dream" becomes "know what it means"
records.note: The Aramaic has the king wanting to know the dream itself, the point of verses 5-9; the GNB narrows it to its meaning.

records.change: "like the Son of God" becomes "looks like an angel"
records.note: The Aramaic bar-elahin can be "a son of the gods"; the GNB interprets it by verse 28's "angel". Many readers see a Christophany in the KJV's reading.

records.change: "a watcher and an holy one" becomes "an angel"; times become years
records.note: Both are the GNB's interpretations of the Aramaic; "times" is not specified as years in the text.

records.change: "seven times shall pass" becomes "for seven years"
records.note: An interpretive translation of the Aramaic 'iddanin ("times"); the KJV leaves the period unspecified.

records.change: "thrones were cast down" becomes "thrones were put in place"
records.note: The Aramaic verb means "thrown" or "set"; the KJV reads overthrow, the GNB setting up for judgment.

records.change: "one like the Son of man" becomes "looked like a human being"
records.note: The Aramaic kebar enash can mean a human figure; the GNB drops the title Jesus takes for himself (Mark 14:62). "Came with the clouds of heaven" is also weakened.

records.change: "whose kingdom... serve and obey him" becomes "their... obey them"
records.note: The Aramaic suffix can be "him" or "it" (the people); the GNB applies the everlasting kingdom to the people, not to the Most High or his ruler.

records.change: "the time of the end" becomes "the end of the world"

records.change: "the desire of women" becomes "the god that women love"

records.change: "a time, times, and an half" becomes "three and a half years"

records.change: "O my Lord" becomes "sir"

records.change: "a wife of whoredoms" becomes a wife who "will be unfaithful"

records.change: "I will utterly take them away" becomes "or forgive them"

records.change: "now the LORD will feed them as a lamb" becomes a question
records.note: The GNB reads the clause as a rhetorical question implying God cannot feed them; the Masoretic text has a statement.

records.change: "like men" becomes "at Adam", a place

records.change: Judah "faithful" becomes Judah "still rebelling"

records.change: "fruitful among his brethren" becomes "flourishes like weeds"

records.change: "a virgin" becomes "a young woman"
records.note: Hebrew betulah; the GNB's choice drops the sense of virginity, as elsewhere in its Old Testament.

records.change: "call on the name of the LORD" becomes "ask for help"

records.change: "prepare to meet thy God" becomes "get ready to face my judgment"

records.change: "Lord, Lord" becomes a single "sir"
records.note: The doubled address is in the Textus Receptus but not in the critical text; the GNB also renders it "sir", losing the title.

records.change: "Hell" becomes "Hades"
records.note: The Greek is hadēs in both; the KJV translates it "hell", the GNB transliterates it. The place of torment is still described.

records.change: Omits "against thee"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus, making the sin general rather than personal.

records.change: Omits "I trow not"
records.note: The closing answer is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in the early Alexandrian witnesses. The question still expects no.

records.change: Whole verse missing
records.note: The verse is absent from P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and most Greek manuscripts and may come from Matthew 24:40, where it stands.

records.change: Blind man's "Lord" becomes "Sir"
records.note: The Greek kyrie is the same; the GNB chooses "sir" as a translation, where the KJV reads it as a title of Christ.

records.change: Zacchaeus's "Lord" becomes "sir"
records.note: A translation choice for kyrie; the narrative still says he spoke "to the Lord".

records.change: Omits "and them that bought"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; the parallel in Mark 11:15 has it.

records.change: Omits "unto the offerings of God"
records.note: "Of God" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; the GNB drops the offering phrase entirely.

records.change: Omits "And the Lord said"
records.note: The introduction is in the Textus Receptus and many manuscripts but not in P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; Jesus is still plainly the speaker.

records.change: Omits "they struck him on the face"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in the early Alexandrian witnesses. The blindfolding and mockery remain.

records.change: Whole verse missing
records.note: The verse is absent from P75, Alexandrinus and Vaticanus and may come from Matthew 27:15 and Mark 15:6, where the custom is still stated.

records.change: Omits the inscription in Greek, Latin and Hebrew
records.note: The phrase is in the Textus Receptus and many manuscripts but not in P75 or Vaticanus; John 19:20 still records the three languages.

records.change: "Lord, remember me" becomes "Remember me, Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Lord"; P75, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read "Jesus" as a name, dropping the thief's title for him.

records.change: Omits "and certain others with them"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; other women are named in verse 10.

records.change: Omits "and of an honeycomb"
records.note: The honeycomb is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The point, that the risen Jesus ate, is kept.

records.change: Omits "praising" and the closing "Amen"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "praising and blessing" and "Amen"; P75, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus have "blessing" alone and no Amen.

records.change: "Only begotten" becomes "only Son"
records.note: A translation choice for monogenēs: the GNB takes it as "only, unique" rather than "only-begotten". Christ's unique sonship is kept but the begetting is not.

records.change: "Only begotten Son" becomes "only Son, who is the same as God"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "only begotten Son"; P66, P75, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read "only begotten God", which the GNB paraphrases. The deity of Christ is stated more strongly, not less.

records.change: Omits "which is in heaven"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P66, P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. It says the Son of Man was in heaven while speaking on earth.

records.change: "Only begotten Son" becomes "only Son"
records.note: A translation choice for monogenēs, as in 1:14. The Son's uniqueness is kept; the begetting is not.

records.change: "Only begotten Son of God" becomes "God's only Son"
records.note: A translation choice for monogenēs, as in 1:14 and 3:16.

records.change: Omits "When the Lord knew"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "the Lord", other early manuscripts "Jesus"; the GNB drops the clause that Jesus knew what the Pharisees heard.

records.change: "In spirit and in truth" becomes "by the power of God's Spirit"
records.note: A translation choice: the GNB reads "spirit" as the Holy Spirit and "truth" as God's true nature, an interpretation the Greek leaves open.

records.change: "In spirit and in truth" becomes "by the power of his Spirit"
records.note: A translation choice, as in 4:23: worship "in spirit" is made worship by the Holy Spirit's power.

records.change: Omits "the Christ"
records.note: "The Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P66, P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. "Savior of the world" is kept.

records.change: Whole verse missing
records.note: The angel stirring the pool is absent from P66, P75, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; it is in Alexandrinus, the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus.

records.change: Omits "and sought to slay him"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P66, P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. Verse 18 still says they sought to kill him.

records.change: "The Father which hath sent me" becomes "he who sent me"
records.note: "Father" is in the Textus Receptus but not in the early Alexandrian witnesses; the Father is plainly meant.

records.change: "The Father's will" becomes "the will of him who sent me"
records.note: "Father" is in the Textus Receptus but not in P66, P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; verse 40 names the Father.

records.change: Omits "on me" after "believeth"
records.note: "On me" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P66, P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus, leaving the object of faith unstated here. It is stated in 6:35 and 6:40.

records.change: "Christ, the Son of the living God" becomes "the Holy One"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "the Christ, the Son of the living God"; P75, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read "the Holy One of God". Peter's confession of the Son is in Matthew 16:16.

records.change: In John 7:53–8:11, bracketed as not original
records.note: The GNB sets John 7:53–8:11, the woman taken in adultery, apart as not original: P66, P75, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus lack it; the Byzantine majority and the Textus Receptus have it.

records.change: In John 7:53–8:11, bracketed as not original
records.note: The GNB sets John 7:53–8:11, the woman taken in adultery, apart as not original: P66, P75, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus lack it; the Byzantine majority and the Textus Receptus have it. Also: Woman taken in adultery (7:53-8:11) bracketed as not original.

records.note: The GNB sets John 7:53–8:11, the woman taken in adultery, apart as not original: P66, P75, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus lack it; the Byzantine majority and the Textus Receptus have it. Also: Omits "being convicted by their own conscience".

records.note: The GNB sets John 7:53–8:11, the woman taken in adultery, apart as not original: P66, P75, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus lack it; the Byzantine majority and the Textus Receptus have it. Also: Omits "saw none but the woman" and "thine accusers".
