records.note: The GNB sets John 7:53–8:11, the woman taken in adultery, apart as not original: P66, P75, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus lack it; the Byzantine majority and the Textus Receptus have it.

records.change: "I am he" becomes "'I Am Who I Am'"
records.note: The Greek is egō eimi in both; the GNB reads it as the divine name of Exodus 3:14, which the KJV does not.

records.change: Omits "the Father"
records.note: "The Father" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P66, P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; "he who sent me" still names him.

records.change: Omits "going through the midst of them, and so passed by"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P66, P75 or Vaticanus, and may come from Luke 4:30.

records.change: "Son of God" becomes "Son of Man"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Son of God"; P66, P75, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read "Son of Man". The man's worship follows in verse 38 either way.

records.change: Omits "as I said unto you"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P66, P75 or Vaticanus.

records.change: "Know, and believe" becomes "know once and for all"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "know and believe"; P45, P66, P75 and Vaticanus read "know and keep knowing". Faith is still called for earlier in the verse.

records.change: Omits "from the place where the dead was laid"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P66, P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus.

records.change: Omits "Simon's son"
records.note: The phrase is in the Textus Receptus and many manuscripts but not in P66, P75, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; 6:71 and 13:26 name Judas's father.

records.change: "Believe not" becomes "do not obey"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "believe not"; P66, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and the critical text read "keep not". The GNB follows the latter.

records.change: Omits "because I go to the Father"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P5, P66, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; verse 17 quotes it, and 16:10 says the same.

records.change: Omits "in the world"; name "you gave me"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "with them in the world" and "those that thou gavest me"; the critical text lacks "in the world" and makes the name what was given to Christ.

records.change: Omits the closing "Amen"
records.note: The Amen is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus.

records.change: "Hell" becomes "world of the dead"; "Holy One" becomes "faithful servant"
records.note: Translation choices for hadēs and hosios in the quotation of Psalm 16:10. "Holy One" is the messianic title Peter applies to Christ.

records.change: Omits "according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P74, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The GNB speaks of a descendant made king; verse 31 names the Messiah.

records.change: "Hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: A translation choice for hadēs, as in 2:27; the resurrection of the Messiah is kept.

records.change: "Added to the church" becomes "added to their group"
records.note: "To the church" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P74, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus, which read "together".

records.change: "His Son Jesus" becomes "his Servant Jesus"
records.note: A translation choice for pais, which can mean child or servant; the GNB reads it as the Servant of Isaiah 52-53. The KJV reads it as Son.

records.change: "His Son Jesus" becomes "his Servant"
records.note: A translation choice for pais, as in 3:13; "Jesus" is also absent from the critical text, though he is plainly meant.

records.change: "Lord, thou art God" becomes "Master and Creator"
records.note: "Thou art God" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P74, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; the address is to God either way.

records.change: Omits "the father of Sychem"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Hamor the father of Sychem"; the critical text reads "Hamor in Shechem", and the GNB drops the place.

records.change: "An angel of the Lord" becomes "an angel"
records.note: "Of the Lord" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus; verse 31 says the Lord's voice spoke.

records.change: Omits "him shall ye hear"; "the Lord your God" becomes "God"
records.note: The words are in some manuscripts and the Textus Receptus but not in P74, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. "Him shall ye hear" still stands in 3:22 and Deuteronomy 18:15.

records.change: Whole verse missing: the eunuch's confession
records.note: The verse is absent from P45, P74, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus, Vaticanus and the Byzantine majority, but is in some Western witnesses and the Textus Receptus. It gives the only confession before baptism in the account.

records.change: Omits "it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus, from the Latin tradition, but in almost no Greek manuscripts here; they stand in 26:14.

records.change: Omits Saul's "Lord, what wilt thou have me to do?"
records.note: The trembling question is in the Textus Receptus, from the Latin tradition, but in almost no Greek manuscripts here; the question stands in 22:10.

records.change: "Preached Christ" becomes "preach that Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Christ"; P45, P74, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read "Jesus". He is still preached as the Son of God.

records.change: Omits "which were sent unto him from Cornelius"
records.note: The phrase is in the Textus Receptus and a few late manuscripts but not in the Byzantine majority or the early witnesses; the context makes it plain.

records.change: Omits "I was fasting"
records.note: The Textus Receptus and Byzantine text read "fasting until this hour; and at the ninth hour I prayed"; P74, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus mention prayer only.

records.change: "Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in some manuscripts and the Textus Receptus but not in P74, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus.

records.change: Omits "Known unto God are all his works"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Known unto God are all his works from the beginning"; the critical text has only "known from of old", closing the quotation of verse 17.

records.change: Whole verse missing
records.note: The verse is absent from P74, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus, Vaticanus and the Byzantine majority; it is in some Western witnesses and the Textus Receptus. Verse 40 still has Silas at Antioch.

records.change: "Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P74, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus.

records.change: "Of one blood" becomes "from one human being"
records.note: "Blood" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P74, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus, which read "from one".

records.change: "Pressed in the spirit" becomes "gave his whole time to preaching"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "pressed in the spirit"; P74, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read "occupied with the word", which the GNB follows.

records.change: "Christ Jesus" becomes "Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P74, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus.

records.change: "Lord Jesus" becomes "the Lord"
records.note: "Jesus" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P74, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus.

records.change: "Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and the Textus Receptus but not in Vaticanus or P74; the critical text brackets or omits it.

records.change: "his own blood" becomes "the blood of his Son"
records.note: The Greek can be read "with his own blood" or "with the blood of his own [Son]"; the GNB chooses the second, a translation choice. The KJV's reading ascribes the blood to God, a text often cited for Christ's deity.

records.change: Omits "that they observe no such thing, save only"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P74, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The four prohibitions are kept, as in 15:29.

records.change: "the name of the Lord" becomes "praying to him"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "the name of the Lord"; the critical text, following the early uncials, reads "his name". The referent is the same Lord of 22:14-15.

records.change: Omits "let us not fight against God"
records.note: The closing clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus; the GNB follows the critical text. Gamaliel's similar warning stands in Acts 5:39.

records.change: Omits "and would have judged according to our law"
records.note: Acts 24:6b-8a is in the Textus Receptus and some later manuscripts but not in the earliest papyri and uncials, which the GNB follows. The loss is narrative, not doctrinal.

records.change: Whole verse missing (Lysias taking Paul by force)
records.note: Part of the longer reading 24:6b-8a found in the Textus Receptus and some Western and later witnesses but absent from P74, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Alexandrinus. Without it, 24:8's "him" refers to Paul rather than Lysias.

records.change: Omits "when he had thus spoken"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in the early uncials the GNB follows. Only narrative detail is lost.

records.change: Omits the centurion delivering prisoners to the captain of the guard
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus. Narrative detail only.

records.change: Whole verse missing (the Jews departing and disputing)
records.note: The verse is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but absent from P74, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Alexandrinus, which the GNB follows. Narrative detail; nothing doctrinal is lost.

records.change: "the spirit of holiness" read as Christ's "divine holiness"
records.note: The Greek is the same; the GNB interprets the phrase as Christ's own divine nature where many read it as the Holy Spirit. A translation choice that shifts the reference.

records.change: Omits "of Christ" after "gospel"
records.note: "Of Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P26, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus. The gospel is still that of God's Son in 1:9.

records.change: Omits "our Lord" after "Christ Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus and Byzantine text add "our Lord"; P46, Alexandrinus and Vaticanus lack it. Christ's lordship is stated in 6:23.

records.change: Omits "who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus, and appears to echo 8:4, where it stands in all texts. The condition on "no condemnation" is still taught in 8:4.

records.change: "firstborn" becomes "the first"
records.note: The Greek (prototokos) is the same; the GNB simplifies the word. "Firstborn" carries the idea of rank and inheritance, which "first" weakens.

records.change: Omits "in righteousness: because a short work"
records.note: The longer quotation of Isaiah 10:22-23 is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus; P46, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus have the shorter form. The point of the quotation stands.

records.change: "word of God" becomes "preaching Christ"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "word of God"; P46, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read "word of Christ". Both name a divine source of the message.

records.change: Omits "But if it be of works... work is no more work"
records.note: The second half is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus (original hand) or Alexandrinus. The contrast of grace and works is still made in the first half and in 4:4-5.

records.change: "God is able" becomes "the Lord is able"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "God"; the early uncials read "Lord". Either names the divine master who upholds the believer.

records.change: Omits "he that regardeth not the day... doth not regard it"
records.note: The clause is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus. The balancing clause about eating remains.

records.change: "judgment seat of Christ" becomes "before God"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "of Christ"; Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and Vaticanus read "of God". The KJV reading, with 14:11-12, ascribes to Christ what is said of God; 2 Corinthians 5:10 still has "judgment seat of Christ".

records.change: "Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ"
records.note: The Textus Receptus adds "Jesus"; the early uncials read "Christ" alone. The same person is named.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ our Lord"
records.note: "Jesus" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus. The full title remains in 16:20.

records.change: Omits "Christ" and the closing "Amen"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Lord Jesus Christ... Amen"; the early uncials read "Lord Jesus" without "Amen". Minor liturgical wording.

records.change: Whole verse missing (the second grace benediction)
records.note: The verse is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, P61, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus. The same benediction stands in 16:20.

records.change: Omits the closing note "Written to the Romans from Corinthus..."
records.note: The subscription is a later scribal colophon printed in the Textus Receptus, not part of Paul's text in the early manuscripts. Nothing doctrinal is lost.

records.change: "the Holy Ghost" becomes "the Spirit"
records.note: "Holy" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus. The Spirit of God is plainly meant (2:12).

records.change: "the Lord Jesus" becomes "the Lord"
records.note: "Jesus" is in Sinaiticus and the Textus Receptus but not in P46 or Vaticanus, which the GNB follows here. The same day of the Lord is meant.

records.change: Omits "and in your spirit, which are God's"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus. God's ownership of the believer is still stated in 6:19.

records.change: Omits "fasting"
records.note: "Fasting and" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus (original hand), Alexandrinus or Vaticanus. Fasting is still commended elsewhere, e.g. Matthew 6:16-18.

records.change: "his virgin" read as an engaged couple, not father and daughter
records.note: The Greek is the same; the GNB interprets the man as a fiancé where the KJV's wording is usually read as a father giving his daughter in marriage. A translation choice that changes who is meant.

records.change: Keeping "his virgin" read as not marrying his fiancée
records.note: The same interpretive choice as 7:36: the GNB reads a fiancé deciding not to marry rather than a father keeping his daughter unmarried. The Greek does not differ.

records.change: "Jesus Christ our Lord" becomes "Jesus our Lord"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus. The question order also follows the critical text.

records.change: "gospel of Christ" becomes "Good News"
records.note: "Of Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in the early uncials. The gospel's content is unchanged.

records.change: "tempt Christ" becomes "put the Lord to the test"
records.note: The Textus Receptus and P46 read "Christ", as does the current Nestle-Aland text; Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and older critical editions read "Lord". "Christ" identifies him with the God tested in the wilderness.

records.change: Omits "for the earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof"
records.note: The repeated quotation of Psalm 24:1 is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in the early uncials. It stands in 10:26 in all texts.

records.change: Omits "Take, eat" and "broken"
records.note: Both are in the Byzantine text and Textus Receptus but not in early papyri, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The body "broken for you" becomes simply "for you".

records.change: Omits "unworthily"; "damnation" becomes "judgment"
records.note: "Unworthily" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus; the idea is stated in 11:27. "Judgment" renders the same Greek word (krima).

records.change: Omits "the Lord": "the Lord from heaven" becomes "came from heaven"
records.note: "The Lord" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The KJV reading names the second Adam as the Lord; his heavenly origin remains.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "the Lord"
records.note: "Jesus Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The Lord meant is plainly Christ.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "the Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Our" and "Christ" are in the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. Minor benediction wording.

records.change: Omits "Amen" and the closing subscription
records.note: "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus but not in Vaticanus and some others; the subscription is a later scribal colophon. Nothing doctrinal is lost.

records.change: "Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Jesus Christ"; P46 and Sinaiticus have it, but Alexandrinus and Vaticanus read "Christ" alone. The same person is meant.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus" becomes "Jesus"
records.note: "The Lord" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in the early uncials. Christ's lordship is stated throughout the letter.

records.change: "Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ"
records.note: "Jesus" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The same reconciler is named.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "the Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Our" and "Christ" are in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The same person is meant.

records.change: Omits "Amen" and the closing subscription
records.note: The benediction itself is GNB 13:13 (versification differs). "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus but not in P46 or Vaticanus; the subscription is a later colophon.

records.change: Omits "which were in Christ"
records.note: The Greek of both texts has "in Christ"; the GNB's paraphrase drops it. A translation choice that loses the description of the churches.

records.change: Omits "in Christ" from the covenant confirmed by God
records.note: "In Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus. The promise's fulfilment in Christ is stated in 3:16.

records.change: Omits "through Christ" as the way one becomes heir
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "heir of God through Christ"; P46, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read "heir through God". Christ's role is stated in 4:4-5.

records.change: Omits "in Christ Jesus"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46 or Vaticanus. The parallel in 5:6 keeps "in Jesus Christ".

records.change: "the Lord Jesus" becomes "Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "the Lord Jesus"; P46 and Vaticanus read "Jesus" alone. The same person is meant.

records.change: Omits the closing subscription "To the Galatians written from Rome"
records.note: The subscription is a later scribal colophon printed in the Textus Receptus, not part of the early manuscripts. "With your spirit" is paraphrased as "with you all".

records.change: Omits "by Jesus Christ" as agent of creation
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus. Creation through Christ is still stated in Colossians 1:16 and John 1:3.

records.change: Omits "of our Lord Jesus Christ" after "the Father"
records.note: The phrase is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus. The Father of Christ is named in 1:3.

records.change: "fruit of the Spirit" becomes "the light"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Spirit"; P46, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and Vaticanus read "light", matching 5:8. "Fruit of the Spirit" remains in Galatians 5:22.

records.change: "fear of God" becomes "reverence for Christ"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "God"; the early uncials read "Christ". The critical reading gives Christ the reverence due to God.

records.change: "the Lord" becomes "Christ"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Lord"; the early uncials read "Christ". The same person is meant, as 5:25 shows.

records.change: Omits "of his flesh, and of his bones"
records.note: The phrase, echoing Genesis 2:23, is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in P46, Sinaiticus (original hand), Alexandrinus or Vaticanus. The body metaphor remains.

records.change: Omits "Amen" and the closing subscription
records.note: The subscription is a later scribal colophon printed in the Textus Receptus, not part of the early manuscripts; "Amen" is also absent from some early witnesses.

records.change: "turn to my salvation" becomes "I shall be set free"
records.note: The Greek (soteria) is the same; the GNB reads it as release from prison rather than salvation. A translation choice that narrows the meaning.

records.change: "thought it not robbery to be equal" becomes not grasping at equality
records.note: A translation choice for harpagmos, not a textual variant. The KJV says Christ rightly held equality with God; the GNB says he did not cling to it, though it still says he had God's nature.

records.change: "trust in the Lord Jesus" becomes "if it is the Lord's will"
records.note: Both texts read "in the Lord Jesus"; the GNB's paraphrase drops the name Jesus. A translation choice.

records.change: Omits "Amen" and the closing subscription
records.note: The subscription is a later scribal colophon printed in the Textus Receptus, not part of the early manuscripts; "Amen" is also absent from some early witnesses.

records.change: Omits "and the Lord Jesus Christ" from the greeting
records.note: The phrase is in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and the Textus Receptus but not in Vaticanus and others, which the GNB follows. Grace from Christ is stated in 4:18 and the other Pauline greetings.

records.change: Omits "through his blood"
records.note: The phrase is in some later manuscripts and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or most early witnesses, and may come from Ephesians 1:7. Redemption through Christ's blood is still stated in Colossians 1:20 and Ephesians 1:7.

records.change: "Christ Jesus" becomes "Christ"
records.note: "Jesus" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus. The same person is meant.

records.change: "and of the Father, and of Christ" becomes "which is Christ"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has the longer phrase; P46 and Vaticanus read "of God, Christ", identifying the mystery with Christ. The Father is not named separately.

records.change: "Christ forgave you" becomes "the Lord has forgiven you"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Christ"; P46, Alexandrinus and Vaticanus read "Lord". The same forgiver is meant.

records.change: Singing "to the Lord" becomes "to God"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "to the Lord"; P46, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and Vaticanus read "to God". "With grace" is rendered "with thanksgiving", a translation choice.

records.change: "fearing God" becomes "reverence for the Lord"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "God"; the early uncials read "Lord", pointing to Christ as in 3:23-24.

records.change: Omits "Amen" and the closing subscription
records.note: The subscription is a later scribal colophon printed in the Textus Receptus, not part of the early manuscripts; "Amen" is also absent from some early witnesses.

records.change: Omits "from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ"
records.note: The phrase is in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and the Textus Receptus but not in Vaticanus and others, which the GNB follows. The first half of the verse still names both.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "our Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "our Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in the early uncials.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "our Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus.

records.change: Omits "Amen" and the closing subscription
records.note: The subscription is a later scribal colophon printed in the Textus Receptus, not part of the early manuscripts; "Amen" is also absent from some early witnesses.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "our Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in the Textus Receptus and Alexandrinus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus.

records.change: First "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "our Lord Jesus"
records.note: "Christ" is in Alexandrinus and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The full title stands later in the verse.

records.change: "the day of Christ" becomes "the Day of the Lord"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Christ"; Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and Vaticanus read "Lord". The Lord is Christ, as 2:1 shows.

records.change: Omits "as God" from "he as God sitteth"
records.note: "As God" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus. His claim to be God is still stated at the verse's end.

records.change: "from the beginning chosen" becomes "chose you as the first"
records.note: The Textus Receptus and Sinaiticus read ap' arches (from the beginning); Vaticanus and others read aparchen (firstfruits). One points to election before time, the other to early converts.

records.change: Omits "Amen" and the closing subscription
records.note: The subscription is a later scribal colophon printed in the Textus Receptus, not part of the early manuscripts; "Amen" is also absent from some early witnesses.

records.change: "Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Lord Jesus Christ"; Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and others read "Christ Jesus" without "Lord".

records.change: Omits "in Christ" from "I speak the truth"
records.note: "In Christ" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or others. The oath of truthfulness remains.

records.change: "God was manifest" becomes "He appeared"
records.note: Later manuscripts and the Textus Receptus read "God" (theos); Sinaiticus and other early witnesses read "who" (hos), which the GNB renders "He". The KJV reading names Christ as God; Christ's deity is still taught in John 1:1 and Titus 2:13.

records.change: Omits "in spirit" from the list of examples
records.note: "In spirit" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or others.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Lord Jesus Christ"; the early uncials read "Christ Jesus" without "Lord".

records.change: Omits "from such withdraw thyself"
records.note: The command is in the Byzantine text and Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and other early witnesses. Withdrawing from false teachers is still urged elsewhere, as in 2 Timothy 3:5.

records.change: Omits "Amen" and the closing subscription
records.note: The subscription is a later scribal colophon printed in the Textus Receptus, not part of the early manuscripts; "Amen" is also absent from some early witnesses. "Thee" also becomes "you all", following the plural in the early uncials.

records.change: "before the Lord" becomes "in God's presence"
records.note: The Textus Receptus and Alexandrinus read "Lord"; Sinaiticus and others read "God". Either names the divine witness.

records.change: "the name of Christ" becomes "belong to the Lord"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Christ"; the early uncials read "Lord". The Lord is Christ in context.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "the Lord Jesus Christ"; Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and others read "Christ Jesus". Christ as judge remains.

records.change: "The Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "The Lord"; omits subscription
records.note: "Jesus Christ" is in the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus (original hand) or others; "Amen" and the subscription are later additions. The Lord meant is Christ.

records.change: Omits "mercy" and "Lord": "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Christ Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "grace, mercy, and peace... Lord Jesus Christ"; Sinaiticus and others read "grace and peace... Christ Jesus". Christ is still called Saviour.

records.change: Omits "Amen" and the closing subscription
records.note: The subscription is a later scribal colophon printed in the Textus Receptus, not part of the early manuscripts; "Amen" is also absent from some early witnesses.

records.change: "Christ Jesus" becomes "Christ"
records.note: "Jesus" is in the Byzantine text and the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or others.

records.change: "refresh my bowels in the Lord" becomes "in Christ"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "Lord"; the early uncials read "Christ". The same person is meant.

records.change: Omits "our", "Amen" and the closing subscription
records.note: The subscription is a later scribal colophon printed in the Textus Receptus, not part of the early manuscripts; "Amen" is also absent from some early witnesses. "Your spirit" is paraphrased as "you all".

records.change: Omits "by himself"; adds "for the sins of all human beings"
records.note: "By himself" is in the Byzantine text and Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus; "all human beings" is the GNB's own paraphrase. Christ's single self-offering is still stated in Hebrews 9:26 and 10:12.

records.change: "I have begotten thee" becomes "I have become your Father"
records.note: The Greek (gegenneka) is the same; the GNB renders the begetting as becoming a Father. A translation choice that drops the word "begotten".

records.change: "the son of man" becomes "mere human beings"
records.note: The Greek (huios anthropou) is the same; the GNB renders it generically and adds "O God". The KJV wording allows the messianic reading 2:8-9 applies to Jesus.

records.change: Omits "didst set him over the works of thy hands"
records.note: The clause is in the Textus Receptus and Sinaiticus but not in P46, Vaticanus or the Byzantine majority; the critical text leaves it out. GNB also makes "him" plural, reading the psalm of humankind generally.

records.change: "Christ Jesus" becomes "Jesus"
records.note: The critical text reads only "Jesus" with P13, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus; the Textus Receptus adds "Christ". Jesus is called Christ throughout the letter.

records.change: "I have begotten thee" becomes "I have become your Father"
records.note: A translation choice for the Greek "gegennēka"; the Father-Son relation is kept but the word "begotten" is lost.

records.change: Omits "after the order of Melchisedec"
records.note: The phrase is in the Textus Receptus and Byzantine text but not in P46, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus. The Melchizedek priesthood is stated in Hebrews 5:6 and 7:17.

records.change: "blood of Jesus" becomes "death of Jesus"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek has "haima" (blood) in all texts. GNB regularly renders Christ's blood as his death, losing the sacrificial image the chapter builds on.

records.change: Omits "saith the Lord"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus and Alexandrinus but not in P46, Sinaiticus (original hand) or D; the critical text omits them. The quotation is still attributed to the Lord.

records.change: "me in my bonds" becomes "prisoners"; omits "in heaven"
records.note: The critical text reads "desmiois" (prisoners) where the Textus Receptus has "desmois mou" (my bonds), and omits "en ouranois". The TR reading points to Paul as author.

records.change: "only begotten son" becomes "only son"
records.note: A translation choice for "monogenēs", here of Isaac; the Greek is the same in all texts.

records.change: "If ye endure" becomes a command "Endure"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "ei" (if); the critical text reads "eis" (for discipline) with P46, Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus. The sense of discipline from God is kept.

records.change: Omits "Amen" and the closing subscription
records.note: "Amen" is missing from Sinaiticus (original hand) and a few other witnesses; the subscription is a later scribal note, not part of the text.

records.change: "the Lord hath promised" becomes "God has promised"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "ho kyrios"; the critical text has no subject, and GNB supplies "God".

records.change: "God, even the Father" becomes "our Lord and Father"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "theon" (God); Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and Vaticanus read "kyrion" (Lord), followed by the critical text.

records.change: "precious blood of Christ" becomes "costly sacrifice of Christ"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek "haima" (blood) is in all texts. The sacrifice is kept but the image of blood is lost.

records.change: Omits "through the Spirit" and "pure" heart
records.note: The Textus Receptus adds "dia pneumatos"; it is not in P72, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus. Some of the same witnesses also omit "katharas" (pure).

records.change: Adds "and be saved"
records.note: "Unto salvation" is in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Alexandrinus and early papyri but not in the Byzantine majority or the Textus Receptus. Growing "into salvation" can be read as salvation reached by growth.

records.change: "the Lord God" becomes "Christ... as Lord"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "kyrion ton theon"; P72, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and Vaticanus read "kyrion ton Christon". The critical reading calls Christ Lord in the place of Isaiah 8:13's LORD.

records.change: "suffered for sins" becomes "died for sins"
records.note: Manuscripts divide between "epathen" (suffered, TR) and "apethanen" (died, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus); GNB follows the latter. It also reads "you" for "us".

records.change: Omits "for us"
records.note: "For us" is in the Byzantine text and Textus Receptus but not in Vaticanus and some other early witnesses. Christ's suffering on our behalf is still stated in 1 Peter 2:21 and 3:18.

records.change: Omits "on their part he is evil spoken of...glorified"
records.note: The closing clause is in the Textus Receptus and Byzantine text but not in P72, Sinaiticus or Vaticanus.

records.change: "Christ Jesus" becomes "Christ"
records.note: The critical text omits "Iēsou" with Sinaiticus; the Textus Receptus and Alexandrinus include it. GNB also reads "you" for "us".

records.change: "Christ Jesus" becomes "Christ"; omits "Amen"
records.note: "Jesus" and "Amen" are in the Textus Receptus and Sinaiticus but not Alexandrinus or Vaticanus, which the critical text follows.

records.change: Omits "for ever" from the darkness reserved
records.note: The Textus Receptus adds "eis aiōna"; P72, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and Vaticanus lack it. The same phrase appears in Jude 13.

records.change: "Jesus Christ his Son" becomes "Jesus, his Son"
records.note: The Textus Receptus adds "Christou"; Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and the critical text read only "Jesus".

records.change: "Jesus Christ is come in the flesh" becomes "this about Jesus"
records.note: The Byzantine text and Textus Receptus repeat "Christ is come in the flesh"; Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and Alexandrinus read only "Jesus". The GNB points back to verse 2, where the incarnation is still stated.

records.change: "only begotten Son" becomes "only Son"
records.note: A translation choice for "monogenēs", which is in all texts; the word the KJV gives as "begotten" is lost in the doctrine of Christ's sonship.

records.change: "him that begat...begotten of him" becomes any father and child
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek is the same, but GNB turns a statement about God and his children into a general proverb.

records.change: Omits the heavenly witnesses: Father, Word and Holy Ghost
records.note: The Johannine Comma is in the Textus Receptus and some late Latin witnesses but in no Greek manuscript before the 14th century except as a later addition; the critical text omits it. The Trinity is taught elsewhere, as in Matthew 28:19.

records.change: Omits "in earth", the other half of the Comma
records.note: The words belong with the Comma of verse 7 and stand or fall with it; without them the Spirit, water and blood are the only three witnesses.

records.change: Omits "and that ye may believe on the name..."
records.note: The closing clause is in the Textus Receptus and Byzantine text but not in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus or Alexandrinus.

records.change: "keepeth himself" becomes "the Son of God keeps them"
records.note: Manuscripts divide between "heauton" (himself, TR, Sinaiticus) and "auton" (him, Alexandrinus, Vaticanus); GNB follows the latter and names the begotten one as the Son.

records.change: Omits "Amen"
records.note: "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus and Byzantine text but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus.

records.change: "the Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "Jesus Christ"
records.note: The Textus Receptus adds "kyriou"; Alexandrinus and Vaticanus omit it. GNB also reads "us" for "you".

records.change: "transgresseth" becomes "goes beyond it"; omits second "of Christ"
records.note: The critical text reads "proagōn" (goes ahead) for the TR's "parabainōn" (transgresses), and omits the second "tou Christou".

records.change: Omits "Amen"
records.note: "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or Vaticanus.

records.change: Omits "God" in "the only Lord God"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "despotēn theon"; P72, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and Vaticanus lack "theon", so the title "only Master and Lord" falls to Jesus Christ alone.

records.change: Omits "wise"; adds "through Jesus Christ our Lord" and "all ages past"
records.note: The additions are in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Alexandrinus and early papyri; "wise" and the shorter form come from the Byzantine text and Textus Receptus. The GNB gives glory to God through Christ rather than to God as Saviour alone.

records.change: "washed us...in his own blood" becomes "freed us by his sacrificial death"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "lousanti" (washed); P18, Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus read "lusanti" (freed). GNB also renders "blood" as "sacrificial death".

records.change: Omits "the beginning and the ending"; "Lord" becomes "Lord God"
records.note: Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and most Greek manuscripts lack the title and read "Lord God"; the Textus Receptus follows a few late witnesses. The same title stands in Revelation 21:6 and 22:13. The GNB also renders "Alpha and Omega" as "the first and the last".

records.change: "Jesus Christ" becomes "Jesus", twice
records.note: The Textus Receptus adds "Christou" in both places; Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and the critical text read only "Jesus".

records.change: Omits "I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last"
records.note: The words are in the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or C, nor "which are in Asia". Christ still calls himself the first and the last in 1:17.

records.change: "the Son of man" becomes "a human being"
records.note: A translation choice: "huion anthrōpou" in all texts. The allusion to the messianic title of Daniel 7:13 is lost.

records.change: "hell" becomes "the world of the dead"; omits "Amen"
records.note: GNB renders "hadēs" as the world of the dead; "Amen" is in the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus (original hand), Alexandrinus or C.

records.change: "by thy blood" becomes "by your sacrificial death"; "us" dropped
records.note: "Blood" is in all texts; GNB renders it as death. "Us" (hēmas) is in the Textus Receptus but not Alexandrinus, so the critical text says "people" were bought.

records.change: Omits "four and twenty" and "him that liveth for ever"
records.note: Both phrases are in the Textus Receptus but not in Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or the Byzantine majority; the elders simply worship.

records.change: "Hell" becomes "Hades"
records.note: A translation choice: the Greek "hadēs" is kept as a name, not rendered "hell".

records.change: "an angel" becomes "an eagle"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "angelou"; Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and the Byzantine majority read "aetou" (eagle), followed by the critical text.

records.change: "the God of the earth" becomes "the Lord of the earth"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "theou"; the critical text reads "kyriou" with Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and C.

records.change: Omits "and art to come"
records.note: The phrase is lacking in nearly all Greek manuscripts, including the Byzantine majority; the Textus Receptus has it from a few late witnesses. Without it the hymn presents God's coming as now fulfilled in his reign; the threefold title stands in 1:4, 1:8 and 4:8.

records.change: "Jesus Christ" becomes "Jesus"
records.note: The Textus Receptus adds "Christou"; Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and C read only "Jesus".

records.change: Omits "before the throne of God"
records.note: The phrase is in the Textus Receptus but not in P47, Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus or C.

records.change: "the Son of man" becomes "a human being"
records.note: A translation choice: "huion anthrōpou" in all texts. The allusion to the messianic title of Daniel 7:13 is lost.

records.change: "O Lord...and shalt be" becomes "O Holy One...and were"
records.note: The Textus Receptus follows Beza's "kai ho esomenos"; the Greek manuscripts read "ho hosios" (the Holy One). The TR also adds "Lord".

records.change: Omits "of heaven" after "temple"
records.note: "Tou ouranou" is in the Textus Receptus but not in Alexandrinus; the critical text omits it.

records.change: Omits "the Lord" and "honour"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "kyriō tō theō hēmōn" and adds "honour"; Sinaiticus, Alexandrinus and C read only "our God".

records.change: "stand before God" becomes "standing before the throne"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "theou"; the Greek manuscripts read "thronou" (throne), followed by the critical text.

records.change: "hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: A translation choice for "hadēs", the same in all texts.

records.change: "hell" becomes "the world of the dead"
records.note: A translation choice for "hadēs", the same in all texts. The lake of fire and second death are kept.

records.change: "out of heaven" becomes "from the throne"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "ouranou"; Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus read "thronou", followed by the critical text.

records.change: "God shall wipe away" becomes "He will wipe away"
records.note: The Textus Receptus has "ho theos"; the critical text omits it with Alexandrinus. The referent is still God from verse 3.

records.change: "inherit all things" becomes "receive this"
records.note: The Textus Receptus reads "panta" (all things); the critical text reads "tauta" (these things) with Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus.

records.change: "do his commandments" becomes "wash their robes clean"
records.note: The Textus Receptus and Byzantine text read "poiountes tas entolas autou"; Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus read "plunontes tas stolas autōn". The right to the tree of life is tied to cleansing rather than obedience.

records.change: "book of life" becomes "tree of life"
records.note: Almost all Greek manuscripts read "tree"; "book" entered the Textus Receptus through Erasmus, whose Greek copy lacked these verses and was supplied from the Latin Vulgate. The book of life is still named in 3:5, 20:15 and 21:27.

records.change: "our Lord Jesus Christ" becomes "the Lord Jesus"; omits "Amen"
records.note: "Our", "Christ" and "Amen" are in the Textus Receptus but not in Alexandrinus; the critical text omits them and reads "with all".
